sections.text:
Large pretrained robot foundation models provide strong priors for manipulation, yet adapting them to target tasks with offline teleoperated demonstrations often fails to cover the contact-rich, recovery, and precision-critical states encountered during deployment.

Existing methods mitigate this issue by augmenting offline demonstrations with human-in-the-loop data or online reinforcement learning.

Despite this, offline post-training adapts slowly because it cannot immediately absorb deployment experience, while online RL typically relies on value functions or auxiliary actor-critic models, increasing both training complexity and instability. We present TIDE (Training In DEployment), a human-in-the-loop online post-training system.

TIDE introduces a provenance-conditioned supervised learning framework that updates the policy online from human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer.

Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, TIDE improves milestone-normalized task progress and binary full-task completion over the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, and performs comparably to the fixed-policy collection baseline while making updated checkpoints available during deployment.

Each task-specific online post-training session, from the start of deployment rollouts until the final checkpoint is available, completes in less than one hour while learning and checkpoint handling run asynchronously.

summary.en: The paper presents TIDE, a human-in-the-loop online post-training system for robot deployment. It updates a policy through provenance-conditioned supervised learning on human interventions and policy-generated rollouts collected during deployment, without a learned critic, reward model, or action scorer. Across four real-world bimanual manipulation tasks, the authors report better milestone-normalized progress and full-task completion than the warm-start policy and matched additional offline demonstrations, with performance comparable to a fixed-policy collection baseline. Each session takes less than one hour.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TIDE，一种面向机器人部署过程的人机协同在线后训练系统。它利用部署中收集的人类干预和策略生成轨迹，通过按来源条件化的监督学习更新策略，不依赖学习到的评论家、奖励模型或动作评分器。在四项真实世界双臂操作任务中，作者报告其任务进展和完整任务完成表现优于热启动策略及匹配的额外离线示范，并与固定策略采集基线相当；每项任务从部署采集到最终检查点可用不到一小时。

sections.text:
Behavior cloning for robotic manipulation is highly sensitive to the coverage of its training data, yet collecting diverse successful demonstrations remains costly. We study reinforcement learning (RL) not as a deployable controller, but as a data generator for downstream visuomotor imitation learning.

Our key premise is that multiple successful solution modes cover a broader range of successful trajectories than repeatedly collecting a single narrow solution.

We introduce DiscoDemo, which trains a privileged latent-conditioned RL generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective to discover diverse solutions while preserving task success.

The trained generator produces multiple successful closed-loop behaviors, which are safety-filtered and exported as a static dataset for downstream imitation learning. Across four manipulation tasks, DiscoDemo produces broader successful-state coverage and improves downstream visuomotor policies in both simulation and the real world.

Averaged across tasks, downstream success increases to 62% from 40% for the strongest baseline in simulation, and to 78% from 39% on the real robot, respectively. These results suggest that successful solution diversity improves imitation learning for a pretrained flow-matching VLA and remains complementary to corrective data collection.

Project page: https://davian-robotics.github.io/DiscoDemo

summary.en: DiscoDemo uses reinforcement learning as a generator of data for robotic imitation learning, rather than as a deployable controller. It trains a privileged latent-conditioned generator with a parallel reverse curriculum and a success-gated diversity objective, then safety-filters and exports its successful behaviors as a static dataset. Across four manipulation tasks, evaluations in simulation and on a real robot report broader successful-state coverage and higher downstream visuomotor policy success. The authors suggest that diverse successful solutions benefit imitation learning and complement corrective data collection.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DiscoDemo，将强化学习用作生成机器人模仿学习数据的工具，而非部署控制器。该方法训练带特权潜变量条件的生成器，通过并行反向课程和成功门控的多样性目标发现多种成功行为，再将经安全筛选的行为导出为静态数据集。在四项操作任务的仿真与真实机器人评估中，作者报告成功状态覆盖更广，下游视觉运动策略成功率提高；结果显示，多样化的成功方案有助于模仿学习，并可补充纠正数据采集。

sections.text:
Humanoid motion-tracking policies can reproduce diverse behaviors, yet connecting independently acquired motions into a continuous sequence remains challenging. Interpolation connects boundary poses without considering whether their relative position, heading, and timing provide suitable conditions for a transition.

A generative motion prior can produce richer motion, but poorly arranged boundaries may cause it to generate excessive locomotion, turning, or another unintended action. We present Spatio-Temporal Alignment with a Motion Prior (STAMP), a framework for connecting independently acquired humanoid motions through a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process.

STAMP uses human motion space to draw on rich motion priors and reuse transition knowledge across robot embodiments. Its key component is a learned alignment model that determines the boundary conditions for motion inbetweening.

Given the two motions retargeted to a human rig, the alignment model ranks candidate positions, headings, and transition durations for the following motion. A human motion prior generates the transition under the selected alignment. The completed sequence is retargeted to the robot and used as a reference to train a motion-tracking policy.

We evaluate the tracking success of the generated transitions on Unitree~G1 and~ROBOTIS K1.Physical robot demonstrations further show that STAMP connects independently acquired motions into long-horizon sequences. Project page: https://childtoy.github.io/STAMP-project

summary.en: The paper presents STAMP, which connects independently acquired humanoid motions through a Robot-to-Human-to-Robot process. After retargeting motions to a human rig, a learned alignment model ranks positions, headings, and transition durations for the following motion. A human motion prior generates the transition, and the completed sequence is retargeted to a robot as a reference for training a motion-tracking policy. The authors evaluate transition tracking on Unitree G1 and ROBOTIS K1, and show physical robot demonstrations forming long-horizon sequences.
summary.zh: 论文提出 STAMP，通过“机器人到人体再到机器人”的流程连接独立获取的人形机器人动作。方法先将两段动作重定向到人体骨架，再由学习到的对齐模型为后续动作选择位置、朝向和过渡时长，随后使用人体动作先验生成衔接动作，并将完整序列重定向到机器人，用作训练动作跟踪策略的参考。作者在 Unitree G1 和 ROBOTIS K1 上评估生成过渡的跟踪成功情况，并展示实体机器人连接动作形成长时序列。

sections.text:
The pace of a robot demonstration is often determined by the teleoperator rather than by the task itself. As a result, the same motion can appear at widely different speeds across demonstrations, and policies trained on such data may inherit operator-specific timing along with task behavior.

We propose to learn a speed prior directly from large-scale demonstration data. Given a task instruction, a motion path and the images along it, it predicts a distribution over execution speed along the path, from which a chosen quantile defines a consistent clock for retiming each demonstration.

Existing methods derive the acceleration signal from the very data they accelerate, so each new task costs another fit, annotation, or pair of predefined rates. A single trained speed prior instead covers every task in a corpus.

We fit a speed prior on both robot teleoperation data and handheld demonstrations in which a human arm, rather than a robot arm, moves the gripper, and use it to retime robot demonstrations to the handheld pace before fine-tuning a vision-language-action policy.

For execution, we pair the policy with a real-time optimal-control layer that tracks predicted action chunks under robot constraints using the predicted pace.

On 120 RoboLab tasks, policies fine-tuned on our learned clocks succeed more often and move with up to half the jerk compared with policies fine-tuned on the original demonstration timing and uniformly accelerated to the same speed.

On a real robot, our policy stacks cups in 3.50s, 1.72$\times$ faster than the default policy's 6.02s while succeeding as often, in 29 of 30 trials. Videos and further material are available at https://mllab.snu.ac.kr/projects/learned_speed_prior.

summary.en: The paper learns a speed prior from large-scale demonstrations. Given a task instruction, motion path, and images along it, the prior predicts an execution-speed distribution; a chosen quantile supplies a consistent clock for retiming demonstrations. The authors train on robot teleoperation and handheld demonstrations, retime robot data to the handheld pace, and fine-tune a vision-language-action policy with a real-time optimal-control layer. On 120 RoboLab tasks, they report more successes and up to half the jerk. In real-robot cup stacking, the policy takes 3.50 seconds and succeeds in 29 of 30 trials, matching the default policy's success rate.
summary.zh: 论文提出从大规模演示数据中学习速度先验：给定任务指令、运动路径及沿途图像，预测路径上的执行速度分布，再以选定分位数为各演示统一定时。作者用机器人遥操作和人手持设备操纵夹爪的演示训练先验，将机器人演示调整到手持演示的节奏，再微调视觉语言动作策略；执行时结合实时最优控制层跟踪动作块。在120项 RoboLab 任务中，作者报告学习时钟训练的策略成功更多、抖动最多减半。实体机器人叠杯实验中，该策略用时3.50秒，30次试验成功29次，成功率与默认策略相同。

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments.

Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot.

We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction.

We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.

summary.en: The paper discusses prospective safety issues at the intersection of vision-language-action policies that adapt to human intervention and federated learning that combines robot experience without pooling raw records. Human corrections vary in modality, safety meaning, and privacy sensitivity. The authors warn that an update improving average task success could suppress a rare safety intervention or cause an unsafe response on another robot. They propose preserving correction context and uncertainty, testing candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment, and assessing leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. The paper offers counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
summary.zh: 论文讨论视觉语言动作策略适应人类干预与联邦学习结合的潜在安全问题，即跨任务、环境、人群和机器人本体共享由人类纠正形成的适应结果。作者指出，纠正在模态、安全含义和隐私敏感度上各不相同；提升平均任务成功率的共享更新，可能压制罕见安全干预，或使另一台机器人产生不安全响应。论文提出三项要求：共享决策保留纠正的上下文与不确定性；部署前在接收机器人的闭环中评估候选更新；同时评估信息泄漏与安全关键证据的保留。作者提供反例和可证伪的评估议程，未报告实验结果。

sections.text:
Humanoids increasingly demand lightweight leg mechanisms for agile, dynamic, and energy-efficient locomotion. Reducing distal inertia through proximal actuation has thus become a common design goal. Yet, compact transmissions that preserve torque capability and efficient force transmission remain hard to achieve.

This paper presents a novel series-parallel leg design combining a knee parallel mechanism, an ankle parallel mechanism, and a nonlinear knee-ankle coupling where all actuators placed closer to the hip.

As the knee flexes, the coupling passively assists ankle dorsiflexion for foot clearance and, as it extends it assists plantarflexion for push-off, redistributing ankle load through the knee transmission. We derive the coupling's nonlinear transmission models and validate them in simulation and on hardware.

The design shows that the shared transmission lets both joints draw on each other's actuator capacity by easing the knee's peak torque demand under load and the ankle's peak speed demand during fast motion.

With the leg's proximal actuator placement, the leg achieves an effective reflected mass of 0.37 kg at the foot for a 6 kg leg, demonstrating very low distal leg inertia for dynamic humanoid robots.

summary.en: The paper presents a series-parallel leg design combining knee and ankle parallel mechanisms with a nonlinear knee-ankle coupling, with actuators placed near the hip. As the knee flexes, the coupling passively assists ankle dorsiflexion for foot clearance; as it extends, it assists plantarflexion for push-off, redistributing ankle load through the knee transmission. The authors derive transmission models and validate them in simulation and on hardware. They report reduced peak knee torque demand under load and reduced peak ankle speed demand during fast motion. For a 6 kg leg, effective reflected mass at the foot is 0.37 kg.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种串并联腿部设计，结合膝部与踝部并联机构，以及非线性膝踝耦合，并将执行器布置在靠近髋部的位置。膝关节屈曲时，耦合被动辅助踝背屈以抬脚；膝关节伸展时则辅助跖屈以蹬地，并通过膝部传动分担踝部负载。作者推导非线性传动模型，并在仿真和硬件上验证。论文称共享传动可降低负载下膝关节峰值扭矩需求及快速运动时踝关节峰值速度需求；对于6千克的腿，足部有效反射质量为0.37千克。

sections.text:
A central challenge in deploying robot policies is inference-time policy steering: redirecting a policy to satisfy natural-language preferences unseen in training, without retraining.

Existing methods fail in two modes: end-to-end policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) require fine-tuning or expert-level guidance, while neuro-symbolic methods rely on predefined symbols whose edits can yield logically valid but physically infeasible plans.

We propose ReStruct, a zero-shot method built on a neural automaton policy that decomposes a visuomotor policy into a high-level state-machine skeleton and a low-level residual controller.

A vision-language model (VLM) grounds the preference in the skeleton's learned symbols, refining them if needed, and compiles it into a temporal-logic automaton, whose synchronous product with the skeleton reconfigures the task structure. With the controller frozen, the skeleton's action priors are updated for physically-aware control.

In simulation and real-world experiments, ReStruct steers preferences from object-centric specifications to temporal-logic constraints, including novel combinations of demonstrated behaviors that require compositional generalization.

Average preference-following success is 70.9% in simulation and 92.5% on a real robot, surpassing baselines like the prompt-steered vision-language-action model {\pi}0.5.

summary.en: The paper presents ReStruct, a zero-shot method for steering robot policies without retraining. It separates a visuomotor policy into a high-level state-machine skeleton and a low-level residual controller. A vision-language model maps preferences to learned symbols and compiles them into a temporal-logic automaton to reconfigure task structure; the controller stays frozen while action priors are updated for physical awareness. The authors report simulation and real-robot results, including 70.9% and 92.5% average preference-following success, respectively.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ReStruct，一种无需重新训练的零样本机器人策略引导方法。它将视觉运动策略拆为高层状态机骨架和低层残差控制器，由视觉语言模型把偏好映射到学习符号并编译为时序逻辑自动机，再重构任务结构；控制器保持冻结，同时更新动作先验以考虑物理可行性。作者报告，该方法在仿真和真实机器人实验中支持从物体偏好到时序约束的引导，也能组合已演示行为；偏好遵循成功率分别为70.9%和92.5%，高于所比较基线。

sections.text:
Flow-matching Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generate expressive continuous trajectories for robotic manipulation, yet balancing real-time responsiveness with execution stability remains a persistent challenge. Standard deployment workflows typically treat numerical solver depth and execution horizon as decoupled choices.

The horizon amortizes inference latency, while solver depth is kept high to preserve integration fidelity. In this paper, we reveal a fundamental compute-execution coupling in flow-matching VLAs governed by a systematic sign reversal.

While coarse numerical integration degrades precision under rapid replanning, it markedly improves task performance under extended open-loop commitment. Geometrically, numerical truncation contracts lateral action dispersion around an invariant trajectory centroid, serving as an implicit regularizer that suppresses compounding open-loop drift.

Across LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world Franka manipulation on representative VLA backbones including $\pi_0$, $\pi_{0.5}$, and GR00T, exploiting this joint coupling consistently achieves superior task success while drastically lowering inference latency, entirely training-free and without architectural modifications.

These findings establish numerical sampling depth as an operational variance regulator, shifting its role from a static precision budget to an active deployment knob in robot learning. Project page: https://jiabingyang01.github.io/Horizon-Depth-VLA/

summary.en: The paper examines how numerical sampling depth interacts with execution horizon in flow-matching vision-language-action policies. The authors report that coarse integration reduces precision during rapid replanning but improves performance with extended open-loop execution. They explain this as truncation contracting lateral action dispersion around an invariant trajectory centroid and suppressing accumulated drift. Across LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world Franka manipulation, they report improved task success and lower inference latency without training or architectural changes.
summary.zh: 论文研究流匹配视觉语言动作策略中数值采样深度与执行时域的耦合。作者报告，快速重规划时粗积分会降低精度，但延长开环执行时可提升任务表现；其解释是数值截断收缩动作在不变轨迹中心周围的横向离散，从而抑制漂移累积。在 LIBERO、RoboTwin 2.0 及真实 Franka 操作实验中，作者称该联合设置在无需训练或改动架构的情况下提升任务成功率并降低推理延迟。

sections.text:
The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data.

We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models.

The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s.

By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

summary.en: The paper presents Flora, an open model suite for robotics data labeling. It covers outcome-reward labels for monitoring deployments, process-reward labels for reinforcement-learning post-training, and timestamped captions for filtering and balancing pretraining data. The authors say Flora is used to train GR00T models and achieves leading scores on WGO-Bench, RoboReward, and Robometer. They report competitive internal benchmark performance against GPT-6 Astra, roughly 125-fold lower cost, and labeling 200,000 hours of data per day.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 Flora，一个面向机器人数据标注的开放模型套件，覆盖真实部署监测所需的结果奖励标签、强化学习后训练所需的过程奖励标签，以及用于筛选和平衡预训练数据的时间戳字幕。作者称该数据引擎用于训练 GR00T 模型，在 WGO-Bench、RoboReward 和 Robometer 基准取得领先成绩；内部基准表现可与 GPT-6 Astra 相比，并称成本约为其 API 服务的125分之一。作者还报告其每日为20万小时数据生成标签，并开放该引擎供研究者扩展数据集和探索新应用。

sections.text:
Collective robotics is split by a long-standing but increasingly artificial boundary between centralised multi-robot systems that prioritise optimality and decentralised swarms that prioritise robustness and adaptivity.

We propose a unified control framework, shifting from `obligate' swarms---systems constrained to pure self-organisation---to facultatively swarming systems: hybrid architectures that operate as centrally planned systems under permissive conditions yet degrade gracefully into decentralised swarming under environmental stress.

By reframing swarming as a dynamic capability, rather than a rigid system category, we outline a pathway towards collective robotic systems that benefit from centralised optimality when conditions permit and from the flexibility of self-organisation when they do not.

summary.en: The authors describe a longstanding distinction between centralized multi-robot systems, which prioritize optimality, and decentralized swarms, which emphasize robustness and adaptability. They propose a unified control framework for facultatively swarming systems: these use central planning when conditions permit and degrade gracefully into decentralized self-organization under environmental stress. The paper frames swarming as a dynamic capability rather than a fixed system category, outlining a path toward systems that can draw on both approaches.
summary.zh: 作者指出，集体机器人研究长期区分以最优性为重心的集中式多机器人系统和强调鲁棒性、适应性的去中心化群体机器人，认为这一界限日益显得人为。文章提出统一控制框架，将“义务型”群体转向“可选择群集”系统：条件允许时集中规划，环境压力增大时平稳退化为去中心化自组织。作者据此主张，把群集视为动态能力而非固定系统类别。

sections.text:
When a vision-language-action (VLA) model is fine-tuned with its trainable weights in bfloat16 (bf16) and no fp32 master copy, AdamW writes each update straight into bf16, silently rounding away any update smaller than 1/512 of a weight.

In 9 of 12 open VLA codebases a default or documented recipe trains this way, 4 on full weight matrices, including LeRobot's SmolVLA default and its $\pi_0$/$\pi_{0.5}$ guides. In our LIBERO runs without the copy, a probe every 100 steps finds at least 79% of updates to bf16 weights erased.

On the Hugging Face Hub, 99% of sampled full-weight SmolVLA fine-tunes store the action expert in bf16, and 84% of recent $\pi_{0.5}$ fine-tunes with a training configuration set the bf16 flag.

On LIBERO-Object, with rules fixed in advance, an fp32 copy raises success over LeRobot's storage from 4.3% to 49.3% for SmolVLA and from 5.1% to 80.9% for $\pi_{0.5}$ at a ten-times lower learning rate, where both models are undertrained, and from 89.0% to 97.7% for $\pi_{0.5}$ at its default rate.

For SmolVLA at its default rate it adds 10.2 points with open-loop 50-action chunks but only 4.2 when re-planning every 10 actions. In these five comparisons and two more against SmolVLA with every trainable weight in bf16, every run with the copy beats every run without it (p < 0.05); all gaps but the 8.7- and 4.2-point ones clear our 10-point threshold.

The fix is to keep the trainable weights in fp32 during training, a one-line change for SmolVLA in LeRobot.

summary.en: The authors argue that fine-tuning vision-language-action models with trainable bf16 weights and no fp32 master copy can round away small AdamW updates. They report this setup in default or documented recipes in 9 of 12 open codebases. In LIBERO runs, probes found at least 79% of updates erased. On LIBERO-Object, retaining an fp32 copy improved success in the reported comparisons, with gains varying by model, learning rate, and planning setup. The claims are bounded by these codebase observations and experiments.
summary.zh: 作者指出，若视觉—语言—动作模型以 bf16 权重微调且没有 fp32 主副本，小幅 AdamW 更新会被舍入抹去；其对 12 个开源代码库的检查发现，9 个默认或文档方案如此。LIBERO 仿真中，探针显示至少 79% 的更新被抹去；作者还报告，在 LIBERO-Object 上保留 fp32 副本可提高若干模型成功率，幅度因模型、学习率和规划方式而异。结论限于所述代码库检查与实验设置。

items.title: Full-Weight VLA Fine-Tuning Without an fp32 Master Copy Silently Erases Most Updates

sections.text:
Human-guided collaborative transport becomes interaction-critical when the operator can continue along a route segment that is not executable by the robot--payload system. In this regime, operator motion is not an exogenous reference: it simultaneously communicates a persistent route tendency and adapts to the robot's realized progress.

A common modular formulation predicts one operator future from observation history, scores multiple robot proposals against that shared forecast, and then modifies the selected command for local feasibility. This can compare candidates under responses they would not induce and can condition prediction on an action that is never executed.

We formulate local control over executable-action-indexed joint human--robot transitions and instantiate it in Consistent Action--Response Execution (CARE).

Each nominal proposal or bounded alternative is first mapped to an executable action; that same action conditions the route-aligned operator-response prediction, the matched robot--operator rollout, and a fixed interaction utility for candidate selection.

Bounded reciprocal refinement handles transient route--feasibility mismatch, whereas persistent progress loss replaces the nominal proposal with a progress-oriented recovery proposal while retaining the same downstream executable-action-conditioned evaluation.

Across training and held-out maps, CARE preserves near-saturated performance when the indicated route remains locally usable and achieves the highest observed success and service availability when the operator can continue but the robot must detour.

It also yields lower jerk-proxy values and measured controller latency than dynamic-window and Timed Elastic Band baselines. Factorial ablations distinguish reciprocal refinement from progress recovery, delayed-response tests probe temporal mismatch, and an indoor deployment demonstrates physical executability.

summary.en: The paper addresses human-guided robot transport when an operator continues along a route segment the robot and payload cannot execute. CARE maps each proposal to an executable action, then uses that same action to predict the operator’s response, evaluate a joint rollout, and select a candidate. It also introduces reciprocal refinement and progress-oriented recovery. Across training and held-out maps, the authors report near-saturated performance when the route is locally usable and the highest observed success and service availability when detours are needed. An indoor deployment demonstrates physical executability.
summary.zh: 文章研究人类引导机器人搬运时，操作员可能沿机器人与载荷无法执行的路线继续移动，人的动作同时表达路线倾向并适应机器人进展。CARE 将候选动作先映射为可执行动作，再用同一动作预测人的响应、评估人机联合轨迹并选择方案；进度持续受损时切换为恢复方案。作者报告，在训练及留出地图中，该方法在路线可行时保持近饱和表现，在需绕行时取得最高观测成功率和服务可用性，并在相关基线比较中 jerk 代理值和控制器延迟较低。室内部署展示了物理可执行性。

sections.text:
Humans manipulate objects within their hands through touch alone with remarkable ease, but for robots, achieving sustained real-world manipulation without vision remains an open challenge.

Although reinforcement learning (RL) can generate sophisticated blind manipulation policies in simulation, transferring them to a real dexterous hand remains hindered by continuously changing contacts, motion-induced tactile information drift, and the gap between simulated and physical dynamics.

We study this problem through Baoding ball rotation on the Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite, using only proprioception and binary tactile feedback as observations.

We achieve successful zero-shot transfer through a combination of a sensor-aligned, coupling-aware embodiment in simulation, tactile calibration, and two novel episodic domain randomisations: slew-rate action limits and STuck-AT Taxels.

On the physical hand, the policy achieves sustained blind Baoding rotation, completing $\textbf{225 consecutive $\mathbf{180^\circ}$ rotations (112.5 full rotations) at $\sim0.36 \;\text{rot/s}$}$ in a single continuous trial without any vision or object-state information.

Furthermore, we evaluate the contribution of tactile sensing relative to proprioception alone and identify the hand regions where tactile information is most important. This is the strongest reported hardware result for Baoding ball manipulation in both rotation count and speed, irrespective of the sensing modality used.

By effectively bridging the sim-to-real gap, our framework sets a new benchmark for sustained tactile-driven dexterous manipulation on physical hardware.

summary.en: The authors study blind Baoding ball rotation with a Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite, using proprioception and binary tactile feedback without vision. Their approach combines a sensor-aligned, coupling-aware simulation embodiment, tactile calibration, and two episodic domain randomizations, and they report successful zero-shot transfer. In one continuous physical-hand trial, the policy completed 225 consecutive 180-degree rotations at about 0.36 rotations per second, without vision or object-state information. The paper also evaluates tactile sensing against proprioception alone and identifies hand regions where touch matters most.
summary.zh: 作者研究机器人仅凭本体感觉和二值触觉反馈，在 Shadow Dexterous Hand Lite 上盲操作旋转保定球。方法结合传感器对齐且考虑耦合的仿真具身、触觉校准，以及两种情景式域随机化；作者报告实现零样本迁移。实体手的一次连续试验完成 225 次连续 180°旋转，即 112.5 圈，速度约 0.36 圈/秒，全程不使用视觉或物体状态信息。文章还比较触觉与单独本体感觉的作用，并分析触觉重要的手部区域；其基准领先的说法是作者的报告。

items.title: No Eyes, No Problem: What Does Touch Contribute to Blind Baoding Ball Manipulation?

sections.text:
Reconstructing the shape of continuum manipulators from sparse, noisy sensor data is a challenging task, owing to the infinite-dimensional nature of such systems.

Existing approaches broadly trade off between parametric methods that yield compact state representations but lack probabilistic structure, and Cosserat rod inference on factor graphs, which provides principled uncertainty quantification at the cost of a state dimension that grows with the spatial discretization.

This letter combines the strengths of both these approaches by estimating the coefficients of a compact Geometric Variable Strain (GVS) parameterization within a factor graph framework.

A novel kinematic factor, derived from the Magnus expansion of the strain field, encodes the closed-form rod geometry as a prior constraint linking the GVS strain coefficients to the backbone pose variables.

The resulting formulation yields a compact state vector, is directly amenable to model-based control, and it retains the modularity, probabilistic treatment, and computational efficiency of factor graph inference.

The proposed method is evaluated on both simulated and experimental data and compared against a Gaussian Process (GP) regression baseline, demonstrating increased accuracy in partial and sparse measurement scenarios while preserving computational efficiency.

summary.en: This letter estimates continuum robot states by fitting strain coefficients in a compact Geometric Variable Strain parameterization within a factor graph. A kinematic factor derived from the Magnus expansion links those coefficients to backbone pose variables as a prior encoding closed-form rod geometry. The authors say the formulation retains probabilistic inference, modularity, and computational efficiency while supporting model-based control. Evaluation on simulated and experimental data against a Gaussian Process regression baseline reports higher accuracy for partial and sparse measurements while preserving computational efficiency.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种基于因子图的连续体机器人状态估计方法，在紧凑的几何可变应变参数化中估计应变系数。方法利用应变场的 Magnus 展开构造运动学因子，将系数与主干位姿变量联系起来，作为闭式杆件几何的先验约束。作者称该方法兼具紧凑状态表示、概率推断、模块化和计算效率，并适用于基于模型的控制。在仿真和实验数据上与高斯过程回归基线比较，结果显示其在部分和稀疏测量场景中精度更高，同时保持计算效率。

items.title: Factor Graph-Based Continuum Robot State Estimation with Magnus Expansion Priors

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as powerful general-purpose robot policies, but their successes and failures remain difficult to diagnose and understand.

In this work, we show that sparse autoencoder (SAE) representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can be used to predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state.

Moreover, to provide insights into what common behaviors may contribute to these outcomes, we identify individual SAE features whose strong activations are associated with specific stages of success or failure, and uncover recurring behavioral patterns by localizing temporal intervals where these features exhibit significant activation changes.

We further develop a VLM-based interpretation pipeline to generate behavioral descriptions of these patterns and validate their correspondence to feature activations on held-out intervals.

summary.en: This work investigates how to diagnose and interpret successes and failures in Vision-Language-Action models. The authors report that sparse autoencoder representations of OpenVLA activations contain outcome-predictive information and can predict task failure before the robot reaches an unrecoverable state. They identify individual features associated with stages of success or failure and recurring behavioral patterns by locating intervals with significant activation changes. A VLM-based pipeline generates behavioral descriptions, whose correspondence to feature activations is validated on held-out intervals.
summary.zh: 本文研究视觉—语言—动作模型的成功与失败如何诊断和解释。作者表明，OpenVLA 激活中的稀疏自编码器表示包含可预测任务结果的信息，可在机器人进入不可恢复状态前预测失败。研究还识别出与成功或失败特定阶段相关的单个特征，并通过定位这些特征激活显著变化的时间区间，归纳反复出现的行为模式。作者进一步提出基于视觉语言模型的解释流程，为这些模式生成行为描述，并在留出区间验证描述与特征激活的对应关系。

sections.text:
Action-conditioned world models increasingly serve as learned simulators for robotic policy improvement, yet their reliability rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect the consequences of arbitrary valid actions. Systematic evaluation against action-specific ground truth remains limited beyond expert demonstrations.

To address this gap, we introduce WorldEcho, which evaluates action following over a broader action distribution through visual integrity and SE（3） end-effector trajectory alignment.

Our diagnosis shows that expert-trained models perform better on demonstrated actions but struggle with off-expert trajectories, producing motion inconsistent with the commanded actions or visually invalid rollouts.

To mitigate these failures, we propose WorldSync, which broadens action coverage, grounds intermediate video representations in action-induced robot dynamics through an Action-Forcing Expert, and aligns predicted and ground-truth changes under action interventions.

Experiments show that WorldSync reduces integrity-gated error on RoboTwin and, when used for iterative policy improvement, yields higher success rates in simulation and on real robots.

summary.en: The authors introduce WorldEcho to evaluate action following in robotic world models across a broader action distribution, using visual integrity and SE(3) end-effector trajectory alignment. Their diagnosis finds that models trained on expert data perform better on demonstrated actions but may generate motion inconsistent with commands or visually invalid rollouts for off-expert trajectories. WorldSync addresses these failures by broadening action coverage, grounding intermediate video representations in action-induced dynamics, and aligning changes under interventions. Experiments report reduced integrity-gated error on RoboTwin and higher policy success rates in simulation and on real robots.
summary.zh: 本文提出 WorldEcho，用于在比专家演示更广的动作分布上评估机器人世界模型是否遵循动作，通过视觉完整性和末端执行器 SE(3) 轨迹对齐进行诊断。作者发现，基于专家数据训练的模型在演示动作上表现较好，但面对偏离专家轨迹的动作时，可能生成与指令不符的运动或视觉上无效的结果。为缓解这些问题，WorldSync 扩展动作覆盖范围，并通过动作强制专家及动作干预下的变化对齐，使中间视频表征贴合动作引发的机器人动力学。实验显示，WorldSync 在 RoboTwin 上降低完整性门控误差；用于迭代策略改进时，在仿真和真实机器人上均提高成功率。

items.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning

sections.text:
Designing effective reward functions is a critical challenge in Reinforcement Learning (RL), which traditionally requires costly manual trial-and-error.

While Large Language Model (LLM)-based methods have shown promise in reward design, undifferentiated sampling and limited use of historical feedback often lead to insufficient exploration of the reward space and optimization instability.

To address these challenges, we propose $R^2E$, a Role-driven Reward Evolutionary framework for automated reward function design that structures the process through explicit role specialization. $R^2E$ employs multiple LLM roles with complementary objectives: an Explorer that promotes novelty to expand the search space, a Guardian that performs conservative refinements to improve training stability, and an Evolver that recombines high-performing rewards via crossover and mutation to integrate effective structures.

A dynamic scheduling strategy coordinates these roles, progressively shifting the search from broad exploration to focused exploitation.

To mitigate optimization instability and provide a medium for cross-role collaboration, $R^2E$ incorporates a Global Elite Pool that retains the best-performing rewards to guide subsequent generations, thereby enabling coordinated interaction among roles and ensuring a reliable and consistent refinement process.

Extensive experiments on multiple robotic tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

summary.en: This paper proposes R²E, a role-driven evolutionary framework for automated reinforcement learning reward design. Multiple LLM roles have complementary objectives: an Explorer promotes novelty, a Guardian makes conservative refinements intended to improve training stability, and an Evolver recombines high-performing rewards through crossover and mutation. Dynamic scheduling shifts the search from broad exploration toward focused exploitation. A Global Elite Pool retains top-performing rewards to guide later generations and support collaboration across roles. Experiments on multiple robotic tasks are reported as demonstrating the method’s effectiveness.
summary.zh: 本文提出 R²E，一种以角色分工驱动的进化框架，用于自动设计强化学习奖励函数。多个大语言模型角色分别承担探索新颖方案、保守调整以改善训练稳定性，以及通过交叉和变异重组高表现奖励结构。动态调度策略逐步将搜索重点从广泛探索转向集中利用。框架还设置全局精英池，保留表现最佳的奖励，以指导后续迭代并促进角色间协作。作者称，该方法通过协调搜索过程缓解优化不稳定；在多个机器人任务上的实验显示了其有效性。

items.title: $R^2E:$ A Role-driven Reward Evolutionary Framework for Automated Reward Function Design

sections.text:
Scaling policy learning requires broad experience and reliable supervision. Robot demonstrations provide high-quality trajectory supervision but are costly to collect. Egocentric videos broaden task and environment coverage, yet motion reconstruction and retargeting introduce noisy action labels.

To address this challenge, we introduce EgoForesight, a vision-language-action framework that learns jointly from both sources by reducing the influence of unreliable action labels and exploiting demonstrated outcomes as complementary supervision.

A joint vision-action flow couples future visual representation prediction with action generation, unifying reliability-aware action learning with outcome-informed representation transfer.

Specifically, reliability-conditioned corruption allocates action supervision across noise levels according to source reliability, while reliability-weighted regression regulates each source's contribution. Complementing this treatment of noisy labels, privileged-future representation distillation draws supervision from demonstrated outcomes.

An exponential-moving-average teacher observes the current scene and clean future to encode action-relevant structure from the resulting scene change. Its deeper representations supervise an earlier student layer receiving a corrupted future, providing outcome-informed structure beyond noisy action annotations.

Together, these mechanisms support effective scaling with noisy egocentric actions. Over the tested range, EgoForesight exhibits steeper scaling slopes than the baseline, reducing real-world open-loop action MSE by 20.5% and improving RoboCasa few-shot success by 8.1 percentage points at 30,000 hours of pretraining data.

After post-training, it also achieves strong absolute performance in both simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation.

summary.en: EgoForesight is a vision-language-action framework that jointly learns from robot demonstrations and egocentric videos, aiming to reduce the influence of unreliable action labels while using demonstrated outcomes as additional supervision. It allocates action supervision according to source reliability, weights regression contributions, and distills representations from future scenes. Over the tested range, the authors report steeper scaling slopes than the baseline, with improvements in real-world open-loop action error and RoboCasa few-shot success. After post-training, they report strong absolute performance in simulated and real-world dexterous manipulation.
summary.zh: EgoForesight 是一种从机器人演示和第一人称视频共同学习的视觉—语言—动作框架，旨在降低不可靠动作标签的影响，并利用演示结果提供补充监督。它通过按来源可靠性分配不同噪声水平的动作监督、加权回归，以及基于未来场景的表示蒸馏来学习。在论文测试范围内，其规模扩展斜率高于基线；在真实世界开环动作均方误差和 RoboCasa 少样本成功率上报告了改进。后训练后，作者还报告了其在仿真和真实世界灵巧操作中的绝对表现。

sections.text:
Many manipulation tasks require a robot to remember what it has done and what it has seen. Frontier vision-language models can plan such tasks without task-specific training, but how such a planner should remember an episode is an open question.

We argue that its memory must keep track of what the planner has done and learned, and must let the planner choose what to look at, since every frame costs tokens; a note rewritten at every step meets both poorly.

We propose LogLook, whose execution-grounded memory lets the system keep the record, an execution log and the model's earlier notes, while the model decides where to look: frames are returned only where it expects a change, and demonstrations are skimmed before it inspects the parts it chooses.

Measured with the benchmark's motion planner, LogLook matches the success of a note-only memory with 43% fewer tokens and less than half the images, and fails far fewer episodes through what it remembered or saw. With direct control, LogLook solves 93.5% of the RoboMME test set.

summary.en: LogLook proposes execution-grounded memory for frontier vision-language model planners handling manipulation tasks that require remembering actions and observations. It retains an execution log and earlier model notes, while the model chooses where to look: frames are returned where change is expected, and demonstrations are skimmed before selected portions are inspected. With the benchmark’s motion planner, the authors report success matching note-only memory while using fewer tokens and images, and fewer failures attributed to memory or observation. Under direct control, LogLook solves most of the RoboMME test set.
summary.zh: LogLook 针对需要机器人记住已执行操作和观察内容的操作任务，提出一种执行过程扎根的记忆机制，供无需任务专属训练的前沿视觉—语言模型规划器使用。系统保留执行日志和模型先前笔记，并由模型选择观察位置：只在预期发生变化处返回画面，先浏览演示，再检查所选部分。使用基准的运动规划器测量时，LogLook 以更少令牌和图像达到与仅用笔记记忆相当的成功率，并减少因记忆或观察导致的失败；直接控制时，它解决了 RoboMME 测试集中的大部分任务。

items.title: LogLook: Execution-Grounded Memory for Frontier-Model Robot Planners

sections.text:
Contact-rich manipulation underlies many everyday human activities, yet evaluating robots on such tasks remains difficult: the tasks involve diverse contact behaviors and are hard to reproduce across laboratories.

Drawing on observations of everyday human manipulation, we identify eight essential skills that provide a practical framework for studying contact-rich manipulation. We introduce ContactBench 1.0, an extensible benchmark that instantiates these skills through 36 reference tasks and more than 40 object assets.

The assets capture task-relevant geometry and contact behavior, can be fabricated reproducibly on consumer-grade 3D printers, and are each paired with a matching simulation model. Controlled task variations in both the real world and simulation enable evaluation of how well robot systems generalize.

We evaluate recent representative vision-only and visual-tactile policy learning methods on six benchmark tasks.

The results reveal that while vision-only policies struggle to perceive or react to contact events, visual-tactile policies do not meaningfully improve their performance, highlighting that contact-rich manipulation remains a significant challenge for current policy learning methods.

By providing common task definitions alongside physical and simulated assets, ContactBench 1.0 offers a shared testbed for developing, evaluating, and comparing contact-rich manipulation systems. The benchmark will be open-sourced at https://jingyi-xiang.github.io/contactbench.

summary.en: ContactBench 1.0 is an extensible benchmark for everyday contact-rich robotic manipulation. Based on observations of human manipulation, it defines eight essential skills, represented by 36 reference tasks and more than 40 object assets. The assets capture task-relevant geometry and contact behavior, are reproducible with consumer-grade 3D printers, and have matching simulation models. Controlled variations support evaluation in both real and simulated settings. In six tasks, evaluated vision-only policies struggled with contact events, while visual-tactile policies did not meaningfully improve performance, indicating a continuing challenge for current methods.

sections.text:
Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback.

We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization.

We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability.

We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.

summary.en: The paper presents ViT-H, a framework that directly generates humanoid reference motions from monocular human videos and improves the generator using motion-tracking outcomes. It uses a diffusion model and direct preference optimization, bypassing human-motion reconstruction and retargeting. An autoregressive variant supports real-time video teleoperation with latency below 400 ms. Experiments on the Unitree G1 are reported to outperform the compared pipelines in motion quality and executability. The authors also report favorable scaling with model and data size, and improved executability from tracking feedback across motion trackers.

sections.text:
Intent recognition in human-robot interaction requires agents to resolve ambiguous natural language instructions by inferring the speaker's underlying goals. Research has increasingly focused on two notable paradigms for addressing this task: structured symbolic reasoning and multimodal input enrichment.

However, it remains unclear whether enrichment-based methods provide benefit in settings where the ambiguity concerns unstated human intent rather than missing observable scene information.

In this paper, we present a comparative and diagnostic study benchmarking FISER - a framework utilizing structured social and embodied reasoning - against CEMIR (Context-Enriched Multimodal Intent Recognition), a method that performs multimodal enrichment by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images from textual prompts.

By evaluating both approaches across four Large Language Models (LLMs), ranging from Qwen2.5-Omni-3B to GPT-5, on the HandMeThat v2 benchmark, we analyze their capability to resolve pragmatic ambiguities.

Our statistical analysis, employing multiple-comparison correction, reveals no statistically significant difference in performance between FISER and CEMIR across any model or difficulty level. This pattern holds across all sixteen model-by-difficulty comparisons, as well as in a targeted ablation isolating CEMIR's narrative and visual components.

Instead, performance is primarily associated with backbone capability and the inherent difficulty of the ambiguity.

These findings suggest a boundary condition for text-derived multimodal enrichment: when the relevant task constraints are already available in the textual instruction, synthetic multimodal augmentation may not provide measurable benefit over structured reasoning on the same text.

summary.en: The paper compares FISER, which uses structured social and embodied reasoning, with CEMIR, which enriches text prompts by synthesizing narratives and photorealistic images for pragmatic intent recognition. The methods are evaluated on HandMeThat v2 using four language models. After correction for multiple comparisons, the authors find no statistically significant performance difference across model and difficulty combinations or in a targeted ablation. They report that performance is primarily associated with backbone capability and ambiguity difficulty, and suggest that synthetic multimodal augmentation may offer no measurable benefit when relevant constraints are already stated in text.

sections.text:
Generated robot videos can look convincing while depicting the wrong interaction: a different object is moved, a grasp disappears, or a placement ends outside its destination. We introduce RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework that makes these discrepancies explicit through task-grounded temporal scene graphs.

Unlike approaches that construct separate evidence representations for different evaluation dimensions, we organize task entities, interactions, and motion within a unified, interpretable scene graph representation.

A foundation-model pipeline identifies manipulation roles, grounds persistent object masks, infers and verifies state transitions and action intervals, and reconstructs manipulated-object motion in three dimensions.

Applying this representation to a generated video and a reference demonstration supports an interpretable RGraph-Eval score with visible-object, relation-change, and 3D path-shape components. We also introduce ShareRobot-SG, a collection of 1,000 manipulation scenes from ten ShareRobot sources annotated with the multimodal representation.

Our evaluation separates graph-generation quality from agreement with human video judgments and includes comparisons with adapted SVG2 and SG-Ego, as well as a benchmark of three video generators.

The framework connects robot-video assessment to the observable entities and interactions underlying a task while making the graph annotations reusable beyond evaluation. Code will be publicly available at https://github.com/SashaDance/rgraph-eval.

summary.en: The paper introduces RGraph-Eval, a reference-based framework for assessing differences between generated robot videos and demonstrations using task-grounded temporal scene graphs. Its unified representation captures task entities, interactions, and motion. A foundation-model pipeline identifies manipulation roles, tracks persistent object masks, infers and verifies state changes and action intervals, and reconstructs manipulated-object motion in 3D. The resulting score has visible-object, relation-change, and 3D path-shape components. The paper also presents ShareRobot-SG and separates graph-generation quality from agreement with human judgments; the abstract does not state specific evaluation results.

Robot motion planning faces challenges in high-dimensional spaces and uncertain environments, often constrained by the need for collision-free motions. We advocate an alternative approach, Environmental Constraint Exploitation (ECE), where deliberate contact with the environment simplifies planning by reducing dimensionality and computational complexity.

By integrating ECE into motion planning algorithms, we bias exploration to task-relevant regions and leverage contact for uncertainty reduction to improve robustness during execution. We evaluate ECE benefits with RRT-based planners and demonstrate their practical benefits in a real-world application.

This work consolidates and extends prior research, showcasing how ECE simplifies motion planning while enhancing adaptability and performance in complex environments.

summary.en: The paper advocates Environmental Constraint Exploitation (ECE) for robot motion planning in high-dimensional spaces and uncertain environments. ECE deliberately uses contact with the environment to reduce planning dimensionality and computational complexity, while biasing exploration toward task-relevant regions. The authors argue that contact can also reduce uncertainty and improve robustness during execution. They evaluate ECE with RRT-based planners and report practical benefits in a real-world application. The abstract describes the work as consolidating and extending prior research, but gives no specific experimental figures or comparison details.

Recent advances in large-scale human motion data, motion retargeting, and motion imitation have enabled increasingly capable whole-body control for individual humanoids.

Cooperative carrying is more challenging because successful coordination requires not only plausible individual motions, but also consistent cross-agent and agent-object relations, including shared grasp, relative configuration, and whole-body support.

We introduce CoCarry, a cooperative-carrying dataset containing 220 synchronized two-person sequences across 21 task schemes, five shared-object geometries, four terrain types, and approximately 61 minutes of motion.

We further propose Contact-Support-Structured Retargeting, which starts from nominal individual motions and jointly refines both humanoids around the same prescribed object trajectory.

Cooperation-aware object-local hand anchors preserve compatible four-hand grasp relations, while complementary upper object-interaction and lower support structures retain object-relative geometry and coordinated support.

Across all 220 CoCarry sequences retargeted to two A3 humanoids, our method achieves 0.9995 contact preservation, reduces penetration duration by 67.0% and 71.0% relative to GMR and OmniRetarget, respectively, and maintains a 100% retargeting success rate. On CORE4D with Unitree G1 humanoids, it achieves 0.9906 contact preservation with zero measured sliding.

We further validate the generated references through physics simulation and multiple real-world cooperative carrying experiments on two physical A3 humanoids, demonstrating their usability for downstream dual-humanoid control.

sections.text:
Swarms of small robots are an attractive way to survey lunar caves and lava tubes. Missions such as NASA's CADRE will fly cooperating rovers for distributed mapping, but only in daylight. The 354 h lunar night drops the surface towards 95 K, and the radioisotope heaters that let single rovers survive it cannot be supplied at swarm scale.

In this study we investigate whether a swarm can instead use its own members as thermal shielding. We train one policy, shared by all twenty robots, by reinforcement learning with an evolution-strategies estimator. The policy receives a single reward, once, at the end of the night: the mean temperature of the five coldest robots.

Nothing in that reward refers to position, spacing, exposure or motion. Two behaviors nonetheless emerge. The swarm aggregates, and robots circulate between the sheltered core and the exposed rim, the same pair of behaviors with which emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter.

We measure the survival threshold, the smallest stored energy per robot at which every robot is still alive at sunrise. Across ten runs it is 155.6 +/- 1.3 pcm-h, where one pcm-h is 7.2 kJ of stored heat.

That is 37% below a motionless huddle and within 13% of a physics-based lower bound, and at a budget where the motionless huddle loses six robots, every robot survives. The behavior needs no shared spatial reference and no robot-robot contact, and transfers from twenty robots to forty without retraining.

Generative policies can synthesize robot behaviors, yet controlling and editing them through diverse spatiotemporal references remains challenging. In the real world, human intent requires robot behaviors that satisfy constraints on where, when, and how actions are executed.

Our key insight is that spatiotemporal control references, such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes, can be viewed as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian action space. We introduce the MAP (Masked Action Space) interface to unify these action references and formulate controllable manipulation as an action inpainting problem.

Our Inpainting Policy (IP) reconstructs missing action dimensions of the end-effector, combining progress-guided alignment with multi-mask training supporting unseen action-constraint combinations. We further adopt a training-free RePaint variant that iteratively inpaints the action during denoising to reduce control error.

On ManiSkill and LIBERO-10, our policy achieves average task success rates of 92.67% and 64.67%, respectively.Real-world experiments demonstrate spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7{\deg}, respectively, showing that our policy can use diverse references to guide executable robot behaviors.

sections.text:
Navigating complex, high-dimensional biological search spaces necessitates scalable physical and computational intelligence to explore beyond local optima through iterative self-play across ideation, experimentation, and automation.

Translating experimental designs into reliable physical execution remains bottlenecked by static laboratory automation and unmodeled physical variability.

To address this, we introduce VERified Infrastructure for Discovery Laboratories, or VERID, a foundational infrastructure designed to bridge the gap between the high-level reasoning of artificial intelligence (AI) agents and complex, error-prone physical realities of wet labs.

VERID is a persistent, high-fidelity semantic digital twin of the laboratory workcell that provides four core services: queryable introspection for agentic reasoning, time-compressed simulation for protocol validation, comprehensive trace persistence for a complete scientific record, and a framework for safe execution.

We present three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures to validate the optical and fluidic foundations of VERID. These studies demonstrate how VERID enables pre-emptive detection of critical errors in experimental protocols, stateful mid-run error recovery and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures.

The simulation functions as a discrete accounting engine, allowing agents to safely and inexpensively explore experimental designs in silico and refine experimental strategies through iterative self-play. VERID also captures structured multimodal experimental data for downstream analysis, knowledge mining and agent training.

We argue that this semantic layer is an essential prerequisite for deploying autonomous agents in the biochemical and biomedical sciences, ensuring data integrity, operational safety, and paving the way for tackling previously intractable grand challenges in biology.

summary.en: The paper introduces VERID, infrastructure intended to bridge AI agents’ high-level reasoning and physical execution in wet laboratories. Its high-fidelity semantic digital twin provides queryable workcell state, time-compressed simulation, trace persistence, and a framework for safe execution. Three case studies using aqueous dye and deionized water mixtures validate its optical and fluidic foundations. The authors report pre-emptive protocol error detection, mid-run recovery, and post-hoc identification of subtle physical failures. They argue this semantic layer is a prerequisite for autonomous agents in biochemical and biomedical sciences.

sections.text:
Coding agents can translate language instructions into robot programs. For contact-rich manipulation, a key challenge is to generate and refine control logic that responds to physical interaction.

We present FORCA, a coding agent that takes visual observations and wrist force/torque (F/T) measurements as input to write Python programs for contact probing and force-responsive motion. Between executions, the agent inspects force records alongside visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise both motion and force-feedback control logic.

FORCA requires no demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. Across five real-robot tasks, we demonstrate its effectiveness in three forms of contact-rich manipulation: improving manipulation accuracy, adapting to changes in object or surface properties, and regulating contact under surface variation and object motion.

Compared with a vision-only variant of the same agent, FORCA improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.

summary.en: The paper presents FORCA, a coding agent for contact-rich robot manipulation that uses visual observations and wrist force/torque measurements to write Python programs for probing and force-responsive motion. After each execution, it reviews force records and visual outcomes to diagnose failures and revise control logic. The authors report that FORCA needs no demonstrations, task-specific training, or simulation. In five real-robot tasks, they show manipulation accuracy improvement, adaptation to object or surface changes, and contact regulation. Compared with its vision-only variant, it improves grasp accuracy and task success and reduces contact loss in wiping and peeling.

sections.text:
Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator.

Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands.

It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks.

During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation.

We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels.

We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings.

Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.

summary.en: The paper introduces DexPort, a portable interface for collecting data with dexterous robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment and records commanded joint targets alongside measured states. An operator moves the handheld device to specify wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate finger movements, avoiding independent control of every joint. Demonstrations are collected in laboratory and unstructured settings, then behavior cloning trains visuomotor policies without skill labels. Evaluation covers four tasks, including object pick-and-place, tool use for screwing, drawer stowage, and bimanual scanning. The authors report over 2,500 demonstrations. Recorded robot commands improve results from 11% to 64% versus states, while in-the-wild data raises task success from 36% to 78%.

sections.text:
Robot manipulation involves localized changes: picking up a cup moves the cup while leaving the surrounding scene largely unchanged. Yet existing 3D visual pretraining methods, including recent dynamics-aware variants, model state transitions at the scene level, compressing the motion of everything in a scene into a single global latent action.

This conflates semantically distinct transitions in scenes with multiple moving parts, obscures dependencies between changing regions, and leaves the learned representation vulnerable to task-irrelevant scene content.

We introduce DynaSlots, an action-free, label-free pretraining framework that decomposes each point cloud frame into a small set of temporally consistent slots and models dynamics at this per-slot level rather than the scene level.

A temporal slot propagation module promotes consistent slot assignments across frames; an inverse dynamics model then extracts one latent action per slot from feature differences, and a diffusion-based forward dynamics model, paired with a self-supervised interaction head, predicts each slot's future state while learning pairwise proximity-and-motion relations.

Experiments on Meta-World, Adroit, and a RealMan RM65-B robot demonstrate that DynaSlots outperforms prior scene-level baselines. It achieves superior success rates in simulation and exhibits strong robustness to scene clutter and unseen objects in real-world manipulation.

Code is available at \href{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}{https://zhucezhanghao12345-source.github.io/DynaSlots-Anonymous/}.

summary.en: The paper proposes DynaSlots, an action-free and label-free 3D dynamics pretraining framework. It decomposes point-cloud frames into a small set of temporally consistent slots and models changes per slot rather than at the scene level. Slot propagation supports consistent assignments across frames; an inverse dynamics model derives a latent action for each slot, and a diffusion-based forward model predicts future slot states while learning pairwise proximity and motion relations. Experiments on Meta-World, Adroit, and a RealMan RM65-B robot are reported. The authors state that DynaSlots outperforms scene-level baselines, achieves better success rates in simulation, and shows strong robustness to clutter and unseen objects in real-world manipulation.

sections.text:
Physical self-reproduction in modular robots remains difficult because a robot must not only move, but also collect, align, dock, and separate modules reliably in hardware.

Taking inspiration from how genetically identical cells form the varied tissues of an organism, we introduce a single standardized robotic module that combines a magnetic docking interface with two actuated joints and folds from a flat, two-dimensional configuration into three-dimensional structures.

Modules of this single design can be assembled into two morphologies: a three-module "trilobite" and a five-module "seal".

Using a small set of discrete motion commands, a human operator steers an assembled parent robot to dock magnetically with a sequence of spare modules, which are assembled into a second, structurally identical individual that then separates from the parent.

Because the parent retains all of its original modules, this is a budding-style form of physical reproduction. Here, we report preliminary hardware demonstrations of this full process on both morphologies.

We discuss the current scope of the system, including its present reliance on direct human teleoperation rather than autonomous control, and outline directions toward autonomous execution of this process and repeated validation across a larger number of independent trials.

summary.en: The paper reports preliminary hardware demonstrations of physical self-reproduction in modular robots. A standardized module combines a magnetic docking interface with two actuated joints and folds from a flat configuration into three-dimensional structures. Modules form either a three-module “trilobite” or a five-module “seal.” Using a small set of discrete motion commands, a human operator teleoperates a parent robot to dock with spare modules and assemble a structurally identical individual, which then separates while the parent retains its modules. The authors describe this as budding-style reproduction. The current system relies on direct human teleoperation; autonomous execution and validation across more independent trials are outlined as future directions.

sections.text:
Free-hand dental procedures are typically repetitive, time-consuming and require high precision and manual dexterity. Robots can play a key role in improving procedural accuracy and safety, enhancing patient comfort, and reducing operator workload. However, robotic solutions for free-hand procedures remain limited or completely lacking.

To address this gap, we develop a haptic bilateral teleoperation system (HBTS) for free-hand dental procedures (FH-HBTS).The system includes a mechanical end-effector, compatible with standard clinical tools, and equipped with an endoscopic camera for improved visibility of the intervention site.

By ensuring motion and force correspondence between the operator's and the robot's actions, monitored through visual feedback, we enhance the operator's sensory awareness and motor accuracy.

Furthermore, to ensure procedural safety, we limit interaction forces by scaling the motion references provided to the admittance controller based solely on measured contact forces. This ensures effective force limitation in all contact states without requiring prior knowledge of the environment.

The proposed FH-HBTS is validated through a technical evaluation and an in-vitro pre-clinical study conducted on a dental model under clinically representative, yet simplified, conditions. The results show that the system improves the naturalness, safety, and accuracy of teleoperation, highlighting its potential to enhance free-hand dental procedures.

summary.en: The paper presents a haptic bilateral teleoperation system for free-hand dental procedures, with a mechanical end-effector compatible with standard clinical tools and an endoscopic camera. Motion and force correspondence, monitored through visual feedback, is intended to support operator awareness and accuracy. The system limits interaction forces by scaling motion references based only on measured contact forces, without prior knowledge of the environment. Technical evaluation and an in-vitro pre-clinical study on a dental model under simplified, clinically representative conditions showed improved naturalness, safety, and accuracy.

sections.text:
Traversability analysis in off-road settings remains a fundamental challenge for mobile robots. Key difficulties include constructing an accurate and expressive local map from multimodal sensor data, and using the map to design traversability rules that yield desirable navigation behavior.

Importantly, this system must be resilient to the limited sensing regime brought about by complex environments and high speeds. In this paper, we present TravSUITE, a traversability system suitable for high-speed navigation in off-road environments.

TravSUITE consists of two major components: 1) an efficient voxel mapper that leverages visual foundation models (VFMs) to build a rich geometric-semantic local map from streams of on-board sensor data, and 2) a unified neural network that jointly predicts traversability-relevant quantities in bird's eye view (BEV), including geometry, semantics, speed and cost.

Our training strategy is entirely annotation-free and self-supervised, leveraging tasks such as map inpainting and inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) to learn both map representations and traversability.

We perform a thorough ablation study and comparison to state-of-the-art approaches, and the results indicate that cost learning and auxiliary inpainting each contribute significantly to planning quality, and their combination is critical for achieving state-of-the-art performance in off-road path planning.

We also design a simple risk adaptation mechanism to leverage our method's uncertainty estimates at deploy-time, and demonstrate that a combination of inpainting and risk estimation can result in 80% fewer navigation errors and 5% faster autonomous traversal speeds in real-world hardware experiments.

summary.en: The paper introduces TravSUITE, a traversability system for high-speed off-road navigation. It uses visual foundation models to build a geometric-semantic voxel map and a unified neural network to predict geometry, semantics, speed, and cost in bird’s-eye view. Training is annotation-free and self-supervised, using map inpainting and inverse reinforcement learning. Ablations and comparisons indicate that cost learning and inpainting improve planning quality, and their combination achieves state-of-the-art off-road path planning. In real-world hardware experiments, combining inpainting with risk estimation yielded 80% fewer navigation errors and 5% faster autonomous traversal.

sections.text:
Resource-constrained robots and autonomous vehicles need scene memories that localize a camera and render nearby views without a desktop GPU.

Scene-coordinate regression (SCR) and 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) fit because they avoid an SfM stage, but ACEsplat-style pipelines are GPU-centered, and moving them to an edge FPGA is hard because SCR is pose-sensitive and 3DGS rendering is irregular and capacity-sensitive.

We present LENS, an edge scene-memory acceleration system on the AMD KR260 that brings an ACEsplat-style workload to a low-power FPGA/ARM platform.

Rather than proposing a new scene model, LENS co-designs the two dominant kernels with the board data path: an INT16 SCR accelerator that preserves pose accuracy, and a bit-exact fixed-point ordered 3DGS renderer that rewrites alpha transmittance as a log-sum-exp recurrence and removes provably useless streamed Gaussians.

All LENS latency, power, and quality results are board-measured. The SCR engine preserves DSAC* localization accuracy at 25.42 ms, the on-board renderer reaches 34.11 dB on Cambridge against ACEsplat's 33.20, novel-view synthesis on RealEstate10K reaches 27.84 dB against 26.11, and all ten Wayspots scenes reach the ACEsplat rendering target.

LENS wins performance per watt over a Jetson Orin NX on every deployment task, by 1.9x to 5.7x at about a quarter of the power, and is faster in absolute latency on localization and Wayspots rendering. On-device training reaches ACEsplat-level quality but not the GPU's time or energy, marking the remaining boundary for a future training accelerator.

summary.en: The paper presents LENS, which brings scene-coordinate regression and 3D Gaussian splatting scene memory to a low-power FPGA/ARM platform. On the AMD KR260, it co-designs fixed-point localization and rendering kernels. The abstract states that latency, power, and quality results are board-measured. The authors report localization and rendering quality across several datasets, and say LENS exceeds a Jetson Orin NX in performance per watt; it also has lower absolute latency for localization and Wayspots rendering. On-device training reaches ACEsplat-level quality, but not GPU time or energy performance.
summary.zh: 论文提出LENS，将基于场景坐标回归和三维高斯泼溅的场景记忆工作负载部署到低功耗FPGA/ARM平台。系统在AMD KR260上协同设计定点定位与渲染内核；摘要称所有延迟、功耗和质量结果均由板载测量。作者报告了多个数据集上的定位和渲染质量，并称其每瓦性能优于Jetson Orin NX；在定位和Wayspots渲染上绝对延迟也更低。设备端训练达到与ACEsplat相当的质量，但时间和能耗仍不及GPU。

sections.text:
Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary.

We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges.

It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks.

Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist.

As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.

summary.en: The paper introduces RobustRLlib, a library and benchmark for robust reinforcement learning intended to improve algorithm reusability and clarify empirical capability boundaries. It integrates 17 representative online, offline, and safe RL algorithms through a unified interface, with evaluation spanning diverse real-world shifts and humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. A systematic assessment across 273 perturbation configurations maps current algorithm capabilities and reveals substantial remaining robustness gaps. The authors describe the open-source platform as a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods and developing new robust RL algorithms.

items.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
