sections.text:
A robot generalist must interpret a scene, act on it, and satisfy every condition of a task. How far do frontier vision-language models (VLMs) meet these demands? We introduce Embodied Agent Arena, evaluating ten VLM agents across Geometry, Spatial Reasoning, Affordance, Task Planning, and Manipulation.

Its 1,000 cases combine 32 established sources with GeoProbe, our 168-case benchmark for camera, motion, depth, and scale estimation. A minimal harness leaves task decisions to the model through source-native interfaces.

Closed-weight models lead all five domains, whereas open-weight VLMs show useful spatial reasoning but substantially lower planning and manipulation success. Beneath these averages, similar geometric errors conceal different scale and shape distortions, and valid region estimates need not identify usable action points.

During execution, agents can achieve early subgoals yet lose object control, bind an action to the wrong receiving region, or stop before the required physical state holds. Additional computation does not uniformly resolve these failures: code repair can restore execution without completing the task, while self-review can reverse correct judgments.

Failure costs also differ: the strongest planners concentrate failed-token expenditure in prolonged body-control tasks, whereas other models fail broadly across procedures. Matched traces show how successful recovery uses feedback to restore a missing prerequisite and advance the remaining task.

summary.en: The paper introduces Embodied Agent Arena, which evaluates ten vision-language model agents in geometry, spatial reasoning, affordance, task planning, and manipulation. Its 1,000 cases include GeoProbe, a benchmark for estimating camera, motion, depth, and scale. Closed-weight models lead in all five domains, while open-weight models show useful spatial reasoning but lower planning and manipulation success. Agents may lose object control, select the wrong receiving region, or stop before a required physical state is reached. More computation does not consistently fix these failures.

sections.text:
Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real.

Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised.

In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees.

On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC).On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines.

Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.

summary.en: The paper studies how regularization affects reinforcement learning transfer from simulation to real robots and derives SMM-AC, a regularized algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function. The authors state that it has strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous-control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines such as Soft Actor-Critic. On real robots, it achieves higher return and exhibits greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics. The authors conclude that regularized RL improves real-world policy deployment through robustness to the sim-to-real gap and changing conditions.
summary.zh: 论文研究正则化强化学习对仿真到真实机器人迁移的影响，并提出基于soft mellowmax价值函数的正则化算法SMM-AC。作者称该算法具有较强的鲁棒性保证。在MuJoCo连续控制基准上，SMM-AC与软演员评论家等基线算法表现相当；在真实机器人上，它取得更高回报，并且对观测、环境和动力学扰动表现出更强鲁棒性。作者据此认为，正则化强化学习可通过增强对迁移差距及真实条件变化的鲁棒性，改善策略在现实世界中的部署表现。

sections.text:
Humanoid robots must coordinate locomotion and manipulation in everyday environments, yet progress is difficult to assess across differing policies, controllers, and task settings. LocoManiLab provides an integrated testbed spanning data collection and generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment.

Its task suite covers 234 atomic and compositional tasks across five household scene categories, supported by 51.5 hours of simulated teleoperation.

The evaluation covers twelve policies with a shared controller across task and scene splits and perturbation levels, two policies across five controllers, and studies of demonstration scale and data-source mixtures.

Success rates fall on unseen tasks and scenes and generally decline as visual perturbations increase, with differences in generalization and robustness across policies.

For data generation, a humanoid motion generation model is fine-tuned for loco-manipulation to study the alignment of its outputs with task execution requirements and its integration into the data generation pipeline. Three simulated loco-manipulation tasks closely match real-world setups, enabling evaluation of three policies in both domains.

Similar policy rankings support the reliability of simulation-based evaluation.

summary.en: The paper presents LocoManiLab, an integrated testbed for humanoid loco-manipulation covering data generation, policy training, evaluation, and physical deployment. Its task suite includes 234 atomic and compositional tasks in five household scene categories, supported by 51.5 hours of simulated teleoperation. Evaluations compare policies, controllers, demonstration scale, and data mixtures. Success rates decline on unseen tasks and scenes and generally fall with stronger visual perturbations, with varying generalization and robustness across policies. Three simulated tasks closely match real-world setups; similar policy rankings across both domains support the reliability of simulation-based evaluation.

sections.text:
Long-horizon robot tasks require retaining and using past information. We integrate Test-Time Training (TTT), which stores context in fast weights, into InternVLA-A1 and Pi0.5 to study action generation conditioned on human demonstrations through training on paired demonstrations and robot trajectories.

We implement memory transfer between the two phases and truncated backpropagation, and examine training objectives, gradient coverage, and contrastive regularization across video, short-video, and single-frame cue tasks.

In our experiments, adding TTT and training on paired data at the current scale did not lead to consistent target selection based on demonstrations. Under the tested settings, shorter sequences, full trajectory gradient connectivity, and contrastive regularization did not clearly improve responsiveness to demonstrations.

When demonstrations were reduced to single-frame cues, real-robot execution still showed a preference for cups at fixed positions. We document the implementation, training configurations, and observations to support further inspection and replication.

summary.en: The paper integrates test-time training (TTT) into InternVLA-A1 and Pi0.5 to study action generation conditioned on human demonstrations, using paired demonstrations and robot trajectories. It describes memory transfer between training phases and truncated backpropagation, and examines objectives, gradient coverage, and contrastive regularization. In the tested settings and at the current scale, TTT did not consistently enable demonstration-based target selection, and the examined changes did not clearly improve responsiveness. Real-robot trials with single-frame cues still favored cups at fixed positions.
summary.zh: 研究将测试时训练（TTT）整合进 InternVLA-A1 和 Pi0.5，通过成对的人类演示与机器人轨迹训练，考察模型能否依据演示生成动作。作者实现了两阶段间的记忆迁移和截断反向传播，并比较不同训练目标、梯度覆盖范围及对比正则化。在所测设置和当前规模下，加入 TTT 未能稳定实现基于演示的目标选择；缩短序列、扩展轨迹梯度连接或使用对比正则化也未明显提升响应。单帧演示的真实机器人实验仍偏好固定位置的杯子。

sections.text:
Hierarchical multi-robot exploration decouples frontier allocation from local navigation, making systems brittle in dynamic environments. Without awareness of execution difficulty, allocators may send robots toward frontiers whose routes are congested or unsafe, causing bottlenecks, oscillatory replanning, and redundant coverage.

We propose VORL-EXPLORE, a hybrid learning and planning framework that makes exploration execution-aware through execution fidelity, an estimate of local navigability and execution reliability.

This fidelity score is used to penalize risky or crowded frontiers in a fidelity-coupled Voronoi allocation objective with inter-robot repulsion, and to arbitrate between global $A^*$ guidance and a reactive reinforcement learning policy during navigation.

As a result, robots follow efficient global plans in reliable regions and rely more on safer local reactions in crowded or changing areas. The fidelity model is recalibrated using self-supervised pseudo-labels derived from recent progress and safety outcomes.

Quantitative experiments on randomized dynamic grids and an ablation under severe traffic show higher success rates, shorter exploration lengths, and lower inter-robot coverage overlap. A Gazebo factory scenario is included as a deployment illustration. The source code is available at https://github.com/21ning/VORL-EXPLORE.

summary.en: VORL-EXPLORE is a hybrid learning and planning framework for multi-robot exploration in dynamic environments. It uses execution fidelity, an estimate of local navigability and reliability, to penalize risky or crowded frontiers and to arbitrate between global A* guidance and a reactive reinforcement learning policy. The fidelity model is recalibrated from self-supervised pseudo-labels based on recent progress and safety outcomes. Experiments on randomized dynamic grids and an ablation under severe traffic report higher success, shorter exploration lengths, and less coverage overlap. A Gazebo factory scenario illustrates deployment.
summary.zh: VORL-EXPLORE提出一种面向动态环境的多机器人探索框架，以执行保真度估计局部可通行性和执行可靠性。该分数用于前沿分配，惩罚拥挤或有风险的目标，并在导航时协调全局 A* 指引与强化学习反应策略；模型还根据近期进展和安全结果生成的自监督伪标签重新校准。随机动态网格实验及严重交通条件下的消融实验显示，该方法取得更高成功率、更短探索路径和更低机器人间覆盖重叠。Gazebo 工厂场景作为部署示例呈现。

sections.text:
For robots to work reliably in commercial and industrial applications, recent advances in agentic coding systems have potential to combine interpretable robot programming with the open-world adaptability of model-free policies.

We focus on "Variational Automation" (VA), a class of tasks that have larger variations in object geometry and pose than fixed automation. Model-free policies often struggle to close the reliability gap for VA tasks, which must be executed persistently and reliably in commercial and industrial applications.

Motivated by prior work on Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) and the Robot Operating System (ROS), we introduce Graph-as-Policy (GaP), a multi-agent coding harness that generates directed computation graphs with perception, planning, and control nodes from a Modular Open Robot Skill Library (MORSL).

GaP generates an internal simulation environment to rehearse task instances with different graphs in parallel to iteratively refine the graph structure and parameters to improve success rates and throughput.

Evaluation with 8 new open VA task benchmarks, 4 in simulation and 4 in real-world, suggests that GaP can achieve success rates that significantly outperform baselines. Details, code, and data: https://graph-robots.github.io/gap

summary.en: The paper introduces Graph-as-Policy (GaP), a multi-agent coding harness for variational automation tasks. It generates directed computation graphs containing perception, planning, and control nodes from a modular robot skill library. GaP also creates an internal simulation environment to rehearse task instances with different graphs in parallel and iteratively refine graph structures and parameters. Evaluation on eight new open benchmarks, comprising four simulation and four real-world tasks, suggests that GaP achieves success rates significantly above the baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Graph-as-Policy（GaP），一种用于变异自动化任务的多智能体编码框架。GaP 从模块化开放机器人技能库生成包含感知、规划和控制节点的有向计算图，并构建内部仿真环境，使不同图并行演练任务实例，迭代调整图结构和参数，以提高成功率与吞吐量。作者在八项新的开放变异自动化基准上进行评估，其中四项为仿真、四项为真实世界任务；结果显示，GaP 的成功率显著高于基线。

items.title: GaP: A Graph-as-Policy Multi-Agent Self-Learning Harness For Variational Automation Tasks

sections.text:
Predictive representations for robot manipulation should connect scene geometry with the state changes induced by actions. Our intuition is that understanding what an action will change starts with understanding where things are: complementary RGB and depth observations ground a common scene representation from which to infer those changes.

Guided by this intuition, we introduce DepState-JEPA, a dual-stream RGB--Depth joint-embedding predictive architecture that connects spatial understanding with action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state, DepState.

Built on V-JEPA~2.1, the framework uses depth both as a complementary observation stream and to ground both modalities in metric 3D space, aggregating shared information into DepState while retaining modality-private features for decoding.

Ray-conditioned readouts predict local features without target depth; after an action-conditioned transition, the same decoders predict future RGB and depth features using the predicted state and fixed initial private features.

Robot-state readouts provide recursive proprioceptive inputs; object-trajectory supervision and calibrated forward kinematics shape state learning through motion targets and joint--TCP consistency. Comparisons show stronger RGB-encoder transfer after RGB-D adaptation, feature completion, conditioned visual forecasting, and manipulation success.

Within-model ablations identify contributions from depth content, metric coordinates, and future-state matching, with additional control gains from FK regularization. The project page is available at https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/depstate-jepa/.

summary.en: The paper introduces DepState-JEPA, a dual-stream RGB-D predictive architecture that links spatial understanding and action-conditioned prediction through a shared latent state. Depth and metric 3D coordinates ground the modalities, while modality-specific features remain available for decoding. The model predicts local features and future RGB and depth features after actions. The authors report stronger transfer, feature completion, visual forecasting, and manipulation success, and ablations identify contributions from depth, metric coordinates, future-state matching, and forward-kinematics regularization.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DepState-JEPA，一种双流 RGB-D 联合嵌入预测架构，通过共享潜在状态 DepState 将空间理解与动作条件预测联系起来。框架以深度信息和度量三维坐标为两种模态提供几何约束，同时保留模态私有特征用于解码，并预测局部特征及动作后的 RGB、深度特征。作者报告，该方法在 RGB 编码器迁移、特征补全、条件视觉预测和操作成功方面表现更强；消融分析指出深度内容、度量坐标、未来状态匹配及正运动学正则化的作用。

items.title: DepState-JEPA: Learning Depth-Grounded State Representation for Visual Perception and Manipulation

sections.text:
Generalist robot manipulation requires a single vision-language-action (VLA) policy to execute diverse skills across scenes and instructions. However, current multi-skill VLA policies often leave two aspects of an instruction insufficiently modeled: which primitive skill to execute and where/how to contact and move objects.

We propose MAST-VLA (Multi-skill Adaptation with Skill-conditioned experts and Trajectory-affordance priors), a dual-conditioning framework for robot manipulation.

MAST-VLA introduces skill-conditioned LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (LoRA-MoE) adapters in the LLM backbone, where skill-query tokens and routing biases guide low-rank expert specialization, and converts a predicted affordance heatmap into a patch-level trajectory-affordance spatial prior for the action head.

On the CALVIN ABC$\rightarrow$D long-horizon multi-skill cross-scene generalization setting, MAST-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance, reaching an Avg. Len of 4.65 over five-subtask evaluation sequences. Real-robot multi-skill sequence experiments further validate its deployability under real perception and control noise.

summary.en: The paper proposes MAST-VLA for multi-skill robot manipulation across scenes and instructions. It combines skill-conditioned LoRA mixture-of-experts adapters in the language-model backbone with a patch-level trajectory-affordance prior derived from a predicted heatmap. In the CALVIN ABC-to-D long-horizon cross-scene setting, the authors report an average length of 4.65 across five-subtask evaluation sequences and describe this as state of the art. Real-robot multi-skill sequence experiments are also reported as validation under perception and control noise.
summary.zh: 论文提出 MAST-VLA，用于跨场景、多技能机器人操作。该框架在视觉语言动作模型的语言模型骨干中加入技能条件 LoRA 混合专家适配器，并将预测的可供性热图转换为供动作头使用的块级轨迹空间先验。在 CALVIN ABC→D 长时序多技能跨场景泛化设置中，作者报告其五子任务序列平均长度为 4.65，达到所述最先进表现。真实机器人多技能序列实验也被用于验证其在感知和控制噪声下的可部署性。

sections.text:
Scaling robot learning to long-horizon tasks remains a formidable challenge. While end-to-end policies often lack the structural priors needed for effective long-term reasoning, traditional neuro-symbolic methods rely heavily on hand-crafted symbolic priors.

We introduce ENAP (Emergent Neural Automaton Policy), a neuro-symbolic imitation learning framework in which a bi-level policy adaptively emerges from visuomotor demonstrations.

Specifically, we employ adaptive clustering and an extension of the L* algorithm to learn the task structure from demonstrations as a Mealy state machine, which serves as an interpretable high-level planner capturing latent task modes.

This discrete structure then guides a low-level reactive residual network to learn precise continuous control via behavior cloning (BC).By explicitly modeling discrete transitions and continuous residuals, ENAP achieves sample efficiency and interpretability without task-specific labels.

Experiments on complex manipulation and long-horizon tasks show that ENAP outperforms state-of-the-art end-to-end vision-language-action (VLA) policies by up to 27% in low-data regimes. ENAP can also distill task structure from the latent space of a pre-trained VLA, surpassing it on CALVIN benchmark with 39% fewer parameters (Fig. 1).

summary.en: The paper presents ENAP, a neuro-symbolic imitation-learning framework that derives task structure from visuomotor demonstrations. Adaptive clustering and an extension of the L* algorithm produce an interpretable Mealy state machine for high-level planning, while a reactive residual network learns continuous control through behavior cloning. The authors report that ENAP needs no task-specific labels and outperforms end-to-end VLA policies by up to 27% in low-data experiments. It also reportedly distills structure from a pretrained VLA and surpasses it on CALVIN with 39% fewer parameters.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ENAP，一种从视觉运动示范中学习任务结构的神经符号模仿学习框架。它通过自适应聚类和扩展的 L* 算法，将示范转化为可解释的 Mealy 状态机，用作高层规划器；低层反应式残差网络则通过行为克隆学习连续控制。作者称，该方法无需任务专属标签，并在复杂操作和长时序任务实验的低数据情形下较端到端视觉语言动作策略最高提升 27%。论文还报告，ENAP 可从预训练策略潜在空间提取任务结构，并以少 39% 参数量在 CALVIN 基准上超过该策略。

sections.text:
Dual-arm robotic grasping is essential for manipulating large, heavy, and geometrically complex objects that cannot be reliably handled using a single manipulator. These large objects often contain only sparse graspable regions determined by local geometric properties such as thickness, edge structure, and gripper clearance.

Prior bimanual grasping methods assume access to a full point cloud of the object which inherently contains this geometric information, but may not be accessible in real scenarios. This work proposes PartialBiGrasp, a dual-arm grasp generation framework that operates directly on partial point cloud observations.

Our model learns geometric features implicitly through convolutional occupancy networks, enabling local reasoning about graspability, collision-free contact regions, and object thickness.

We leverage this understanding to generate force-closure compliant grasp pairs, which are further refined using a sampling-based optimization to correct for ambiguity caused by incomplete geometry.

We evaluate our approach using analytical force-closure metrics, large-scale simulation experiments, and real-world robot evaluations on noisy partial point clouds of novel objects, demonstrating robust and physically stable dual-arm grasp generation.

summary.en: The paper proposes PartialBiGrasp, a dual-arm grasp-generation framework that uses partial point clouds, addressing settings where full object scans may be unavailable. Convolutional occupancy networks learn implicit geometric features to reason about graspability, collision-free contact regions, and object thickness. The system generates force-closure-compliant grasp pairs and refines them with sampling-based optimization to address ambiguity from incomplete geometry. Evaluation includes analytical force-closure metrics, large-scale simulations, and real-robot tests on noisy partial views of novel objects; the authors report robust, physically stable grasp generation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PartialBiGrasp，一种直接利用部分点云观测生成双臂抓取的框架，针对大型物体完整点云在实际场景中可能无法获得的问题。模型以卷积占据网络隐式学习几何特征，推断局部可抓取性、无碰撞接触区域和物体厚度，据此生成满足力闭合条件的抓取对，再通过基于采样的优化缓解几何不完整带来的歧义。评估包括解析力闭合指标、大规模仿真实验及新物体噪声部分点云上的真实机器人测试；作者称结果显示抓取生成稳健且物理稳定。

items.title: PartialBiGrasp: Inferring Hidden Local Geometry for Bimanual Grasping from Partial Views

sections.text:
Autonomous mobile robots support material transport in warehouses and industrial facilities, where navigation must adapt to changing operating conditions. Sensor observations reveal physical obstacles, but do not by themselves specify temporary access rules, route preferences, or exceptions known to operators.

This paper presents a natural-language policy interface that brings this knowledge into ROS 2 Nav2.A local large language model converts instructions into JSON policies specifying destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions.

Deterministic checks govern mission acceptance, and three costmap adapters project accepted policies into the existing navigation stack without changing its planner or controller.

On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four local models produce 107-142 correct accepted policies, compared with 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3-20 incorrect acceptances per model. Fault injection records rejection of eight endpoint/JSON faults and 29 validator-stage faults.

Navigation experiments use correct task policies to evaluate keepouts, zone costs, person-dependent regions, and event-conditioned passage in simulation and on a TurtleBot3.For Tasks 1-3, mean travel times are 18.4-24.5% lower in simulation and 23.1-35.0% lower on the physical testbed than with the baseline lacking those policies.

A native KeepoutFilter comparison and two-robot demonstrations examine basic keepout behavior and shared policy projection. The interface connects operator instructions to explicit navigation policies while retaining Nav2's planning and control components.

summary.en: The paper presents an interface that converts natural-language instructions into JSON navigation policies for ROS 2 Nav2. A local language model specifies destinations, spatial constraints, and temporal or event conditions; deterministic checks govern acceptance, and three costmap adapters apply accepted policies without changing the planner or controller. On 150 researcher-authored English commands, four models correctly accepted 107–142 policies, versus 44 for a rule-based parser, with 3–20 incorrect acceptances per model. Simulation and TurtleBot3 experiments compared task travel times with a baseline.
summary.zh: 本文提出将自然语言指令转换为 ROS 2 Nav2 导航策略的接口：本地大语言模型生成包含目的地、空间约束及时间或事件条件的 JSON 策略，经确定性检查后由三个代价地图适配器接入现有导航栈，不改变规划器或控制器。150 条研究者编写的英文指令测试显示，四种模型正确接受 107 至 142 条策略，规则解析器为 44 条；各模型有 3 至 20 条错误接受。仿真和 TurtleBot3 实验还比较了采用策略与基线的任务耗时。

sections.text:
Safe human--robot collaboration requires more than visual description: a monitor must determine whether the robot body is safely separated, already colliding with the scene or a person, or about to collide.

We call this capability collision grounding: binding visual observations to robot body geometry, camera viewpoint, scene layout, human proximity, and temporal motion in order to infer present and imminent contact. We introduce TouchSafeBench, a physics-grounded benchmark for evaluating collision grounding in vision-language models (VLMs).

Built in Habitat~3.0, TouchSafeBench contains 2,940 simulated indoor co-presence episodes across social navigation and social rearrangement, with synchronized multi-view RGB-D observations, top-down trajectory maps, calibrated camera metadata, and simulator-derived contact labels.

We study two deployment-facing tasks: classifying the current safety state and warning about imminent collision before contact.

Across three frontier or robotics-oriented VLMs and nine visual representations, current models remain far from reliable: the best average Macro-F1 stays below 50\%, explicit depth is not automatically transformed into robot-body collision evidence, and robot--scene contact is consistently harder than human-contact risk.

TouchSafeBench reveals a central limitation of embodied VLMs: visual fluency does not imply physical accountability. Reliable robot safety monitors will need representations that explicitly bind viewpoint, robot morphology, metric geometry, and future collision. The benchmark is available at https://jun25336-bit.github.io/TouchSafeBench/ .

summary.en: The paper introduces TouchSafeBench for evaluating whether vision-language models can relate visual observations to robot geometry, viewpoint, scene layout, human proximity, and motion to identify current or imminent collisions. Built in Habitat 3.0, the benchmark has 2,940 simulated indoor co-presence episodes across social navigation and rearrangement, with multi-view RGB-D observations and simulator-derived contact labels. Evaluation of three models and nine visual representations found that the best average Macro-F1 remained below 50%; explicit depth did not automatically provide evidence of robot-body collision, and robot–scene contact was harder to assess than human-contact risk.
summary.zh: 本文提出 TouchSafeBench，用于评估视觉语言模型将视觉观察与机器人几何、视角、场景布局、人类距离及运动信息关联，以判断当前或即将发生的碰撞。该基准在 Habitat 3.0 中包含 2,940 个模拟室内共处片段，覆盖社交导航与物品整理，并提供多视角 RGB-D 观察及模拟器接触标签。对三种模型和九种视觉表示的评估显示，最佳平均 Macro-F1 低于 50%；显式深度信息未必转化为机器人身体碰撞证据，机器人与场景接触也比人类接触风险更难判断。

sections.text:
Swarm morphogenesis requires robots to assemble desired shapes through local interactions. We present a modular framework integrating neural cellular automata (NCA) with existing site selection and collision-aware control. Within this framework, we introduce a decentralized attachment-site discovery mechanism.

Robots already in the formation update and share local NCA states to identify new attachment sites, enabling progressive growth without a predefined list of sites during deployment.

To bridge the mismatch between conventional NCA growth and gradual physical assembly, we additionally propose offline sparse-retention fine-tuning that simulates partial attachment, together with a false-positive loss that penalizes invalid site activations.

Simulations demonstrate formation of diverse lattice morphologies, scaling to several hundred robots, and substantial improvements in morphology accuracy from the proposed fine-tuning. Experiments with Crazyflie quadrotors validate the integrated execution pipeline using robot-relative observations reconstructed from external tracking.

summary.en: The paper presents a swarm morphogenesis framework combining neural cellular automata with existing site selection and collision-aware control, and adds decentralized attachment-site discovery. Robots in a formation share local states to identify new sites for progressive growth without a predefined deployment list. The authors also propose offline sparse-retention fine-tuning to simulate partial attachment and a loss that penalizes invalid site activations. Simulations show diverse lattice morphologies, scaling to several hundred robots, and improved morphology accuracy with fine-tuning. Crazyflie quadrotor experiments validate the integrated execution pipeline.
summary.zh: 本文提出将神经元胞自动机与既有站点选择和避碰控制结合的群体形态生成框架，并设计去中心化附着点发现机制。已在编队中的机器人更新并共享局部状态，以逐步识别新附着点，无需部署时预先列出站点。作者还提出离线稀疏保留微调，以模拟部分附着，并加入惩罚无效站点激活的损失。仿真展示了多种晶格形态及扩展至数百台机器人的能力，并显示微调可提升形态精度；Crazyflie 四旋翼实验验证了集成执行流程。

sections.text:
Recent robot manipulation policies commonly predict continuous action chunks directly from observations, without explicitly modeling reusable structure in the action space. However, manipulation demonstrations often contain recurring short-horizon motion patterns that are shared across tasks.

We introduce \textsc{RoboCode}, which learns these patterns through a shared soft-gated primitive action interface. Rather than assigning each action chunk to a single discrete code, \textsc{RoboCode} represents it as a soft composition of multiple learned primitives, providing a flexible intermediate representation of short-horizon actions.

The primitive interface is learned from action chunks pooled across multiple tasks and then frozen while task-specific state encoders are trained to map current state inputs into the shared latent space. Experiments on five ManiSkill manipulation tasks address three questions.

First, the learned primitive interface reconstructs action chunks with an average reconstruction MSE of 0.0187.Second, analysis of code activations reveals structured code reuse across tasks.

Third, \textsc{RoboCode} achieves the highest or tied closed-loop success rate on all evaluated tasks, with an average success rate of 75.6%, compared with 68.8% for ACT and 41.6% for the larger Diffusion Policy baseline.

These results suggest that soft-gated primitive codebooks provide an effective and interpretable intermediate action representation for robot manipulation.

summary.en: RoboCode learns a shared, soft-gated interface of reusable action primitives from action chunks pooled across tasks. Each short-horizon action is represented as a composition of primitives, and task-specific state encoders are trained after the interface is frozen. In experiments on five ManiSkill manipulation tasks, the authors report an average reconstruction MSE of 0.0187 and structured code reuse across tasks. RoboCode has the highest or tied closed-loop success rate on each evaluated task, averaging 75.6%.

sections.text:
Robotic minimally invasive surgery offers well-documented clinical benefits, but the cost and infrastructure requirements of purpose-built platforms limit access in rural and lower-resourced facilities.

Recent work has teleoperated general-purpose robots for laparoscopic tasks and in vivo procedures, but relied on handheld instruments coupled through passive linkages rather than native robotic actuation. Instead, we adapt da Vinci Classic and Xi instruments onto general-purpose robots that can integrate in clinical workflows.

We present DASH, a da Vinci Adapter for Serial-link and Humanoid platforms, consisting of two types of adapters that require no modification to the instruments themselves.

Each adapter is compatible with many robotic platform load capacities, engages the instrument's native latch, and wirelessly identifies inserted tools to load instrument-specific kinematics and coupling matrices. Teleoperated experiments demonstrate the efficacy of DASH and its benefits for enabling research access to surgical robotic platforms.

summary.en: DASH adapts da Vinci Classic and Xi instruments for use with general-purpose serial-link and humanoid robots. It consists of two adapter types and requires no changes to the instruments. The adapters support various robot load capacities, engage each instrument’s native latch, and wirelessly identify inserted tools so that instrument-specific kinematics and coupling matrices can be loaded. Teleoperated experiments demonstrate the adapters’ efficacy and their potential to broaden research access to surgical robotic platforms.
summary.zh: DASH将da Vinci Classic和Xi手术器械适配到通用串联机器人及人形机器人平台，旨在降低手术机器人研究的平台可及性门槛。该方案包含两类适配器，无需改动器械本身；适配器可匹配多种机器人负载能力，连接器械原生锁扣，并通过无线方式识别插入工具，以载入对应的运动学和耦合矩阵。遥操作实验展示了DASH的有效性及其对手术机器人研究的支持作用。

items.title: DASH: A da Vinci Adapter for Serial-link and Humanoid Robots as an Accessible Platform for Surgical Robotics Research

sections.text:
Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for learning robot behaviors aligned with human intent. However, its scalability is fundamentally limited by the need to collect expensive human preference labels for every new task.

In this work, we present PrefO2O, an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework that enables zero-shot PbRL on unseen target tasks without requiring any human feedback.

The core idea is to learn a task-invariant latent preference space from a small amount of offline preference data on source tasks, where transferable preference structures are disentangled from task-specific variations.

This learned manifold allows PrefO2O to transfer preference structures and reward priors to new tasks under distribution shift, while confidence-weighted optimal transport alignment generates reliable pseudo-preference supervision for online reward adaptation.

Extensive experiments on robotic manipulation and locomotion benchmarks demonstrate that PrefO2O substantially outperforms existing preference-transfer baselines and matches or exceeds PbRL methods trained with real human feedback, while generalizing across multi-to-one and one-to-one transfer settings as well as across different robot embodiments.

summary.en: PrefO2O is an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework intended to enable zero-shot preference-based reinforcement learning on unseen tasks without new human feedback. It learns a task-invariant preference space from limited offline preference data on source tasks, then uses confidence-weighted optimal transport alignment to produce pseudo-preference supervision for online reward adaptation. Experiments on robotic manipulation and locomotion benchmarks report that PrefO2O outperforms existing preference-transfer baselines and matches or exceeds methods trained with real human feedback across the evaluated transfer settings and robot embodiments.
summary.zh: PrefO2O面向新任务中昂贵的人类偏好标注需求，提出离线到在线的潜在偏好迁移框架，目标是在未见目标任务上实现无需人类反馈的零样本偏好强化学习。它从少量源任务离线偏好数据中学习任务不变的潜在偏好空间，并通过置信度加权的最优传输对齐生成伪偏好监督，用于在线奖励适配。作者报告，在机器人操作和运动基准及多种迁移设置中，该方法优于现有偏好迁移基线，并匹配或超过使用真实人类反馈训练的方法。

sections.text:
Robots deployed in human-centric environments routinely receive natural-language descriptions of spatial information ("I left my backpack on the table") that reference parts of the world beyond their perceptual field of view.

Traditional metric-semantic mapping ignores this signal, while off-the-shelf multimodal models remain limited in 3D spatial reasoning and are not directly amenable to fusion with other sensor modalities.

To convert language observations into a calibrated spatial distribution, we train a Language Sensor Model (LSM) that maps each utterance and its scene-graph context to a multimodal distribution, with mixture weights encoding referential ambiguity (e.g., which table) and component covariances encoding spatial uncertainty (e.g., where on the table the target lies).

We then introduce VL-Map (Vision-Language Metric-Semantic Mapping), a probabilistic framework that treats these language predictions as stochastic observations and fuses them with onboard perception within a unified belief map.

On the VLA-3D benchmark as well as on a real-world mobile robot, LSM is the only language predictor whose covariance estimates remain within the calibrated regime; fused into VL-Map, it leads to more accurate predictions of the target object location (about 70% more probability mass on the true target compared to the strongest foundation-model baseline).

Project website: https://aryan-naveen.github.io/language-as-a-sensor/

summary.en: The paper presents the Language Sensor Model (LSM), which maps an utterance and scene-graph context to a calibrated multimodal spatial distribution. Mixture weights represent ambiguity about the referent, while component covariances represent location uncertainty. VL-Map treats language predictions as stochastic observations and fuses them with onboard perception in a unified belief map. On the VLA-3D benchmark and a real-world mobile robot, the authors report calibrated covariance estimates for LSM and about 70% more probability mass on the true target location than the strongest foundation-model baseline after fusion.
summary.zh: 本文将自然语言描述作为空间观测，提出语言传感器模型LSM，将话语及场景图上下文映射为经过校准的多模态空间分布，其中混合权重表示指称歧义，协方差表示位置不确定性。VL-Map将语言预测视为随机观测，并与机器人自身感知融合到统一信念地图中。在VLA-3D基准和真实移动机器人实验中，作者报告LSM的协方差估计保持在校准范围内；融合后的目标位置预测相较最强基础模型基线，在真实目标上的概率质量约高70%。

items.title: Language as a Sensor: Calibrated Spatial Belief Estimation in 3D Scenes from Natural Language

sections.text:
HoloBoxing presents a simple recipe for learning humanoid boxing by building on a pretrained whole-body controller. The recipe separates reusable motor skills from task decisions: a compact planner requests future body-point targets, while the frozen controller handles joint-level execution.

A learned decoder maps 32-dimensional actions to structured target windows, and measured-state imitation initializes the planner before reinforcement learning. Task learning then refines interaction behavior while reusing the decoder and controller, avoiding the need to relearn whole-body control.

This combination keeps task optimization focused on a compact upper policy and supplies an initial behavior before reward-driven exploration. Starting from that available controller, the recipe accounts for about seven minutes of additional training, including reused representation fitting and a single-GPU task run.

This excludes controller pretraining, data preparation, evaluation, and search. Simulated boxing experiments and component controls evaluate the resulting behavior and the roles of imitation initialization and the target representation.

items.title: HoloBoxing: A Simple Recipe for Humanoid Boxing with 7 Minutes of Single-GPU Training

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models inherit rich semantic representations from pretrained Vision-Language Models, yet fine-tuning on limited robot demonstrations degrades this structure and undermines generalization. A fundamental question therefore arises: what constitutes a good action representation?

Inspired by the mirror neuron theory's insight that observation and execution share an intention-level encoding, we examine whether a robot's action representations preserve the semantic structure captured by pretrained encoders.

Systematic probing confirms that this structure erodes during finetuning, and that its quality synchronizes with both task success and out-of-distribution generalization.

We further introduce a plug-and-play method that anchors action representations to a semantic manifold while decomposing representations into a shared semantic channel and a private channel, all discarded at inference, leaving the deployed model unchanged.

Validated on different VLA backbones across simulation and real-world benchmarks, our method yields up to +18.7% on real-world in-distribution tasks and +21.5% on out-of-distribution generalization.

sections.text:
Trajectory optimization is a cornerstone of modern robot autonomy, enabling systems to compute trajectories and controls in real-time while respecting safety and physical constraints. However, it has seen limited usage in spaceflight applications due to its heavy computational demands that exceed the capability of most flight computers.

In this work, we provide results on the first in-space demonstration of using machine learning-based warm starts for accelerating trajectory optimization for the Astrobee free-flying robot onboard the International Space Station (ISS).

We formulate a data-driven optimal control approach that trains a neural network to learn the structure of the trajectory generation problem being solved using sequential convex programming (SCP).

Onboard, this trained neural network predicts solutions for the trajectory generation problem and relies on using the SCP solver to enforce safety constraints for the system.

Our trained network reduces the number of solver iterations required for convergence in cases including rotational dynamics by 60% and in cases with obstacles drawn from the training distribution of the warm start model by 50%.

This work represents a significant milestone in the use of learning-based control for spaceflight applications and a stepping stone for future advances in the use of machine learning for autonomous guidance, navigation, & control.

items.title: Deep Learning Warm Starts for Trajectory Optimization on the International Space Station

sections.text:
Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained on broad, diverse datasets and subsequently fine-tuned on a comparatively small dataset tailored to a specific target robot. Such adaptation recipe is now widely established, achieving its most mature results on fixed-base arms due to their static base dynamics and consistent reference frame.

Mounting the same arm on a quadruped extends the workspace to the entire floor, but fundamentally changes the embodiment: rather than controlling the arm in isolation, the policy must jointly coordinate base navigation, body posture, and end-effector motion.

In this work, we study the practical demands of this embodiment change across data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation on a Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm.

We report the choices that made this real-robot deployment feasible, namely model variant, action horizon, and demonstration conventions, together with a study tailored to a pick-and-place task, separating data coverage from model capacity.

We show that expanding demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%, and incorporating secondary skills (such as pushing rather than grasping) introduces new behavioral modes without degrading baseline performance.

Finally, closed-loop real-world experiments show how dataset composition shapes success and failure, validating the pipeline for more complex loco-manipulation.

summary.en: This work studies closed-loop loco-manipulation with a VLA model on a Unitree Go2 quadruped carrying an AgileX Piper arm. It examines data collection, model adaptation, and inference design, reporting choices such as model variant, action horizon, and demonstration conventions. In a real-robot pick-and-place study, the authors report that broader demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%. Adding secondary skills, including pushing, introduces new behaviors without degrading baseline performance.
summary.zh: 本文研究将视觉-语言-动作模型部署到搭载 AgileX Piper 机械臂的 Unitree Go2 四足机器人上，重点考察数据采集、模型适配与推理设计如何支持闭环移动操作。作者报告了模型版本、动作时域和示范规范等部署选择，并以抓取放置任务分析数据覆盖与模型容量。真实机器人实验显示，扩大示范覆盖可使留出末端执行器误差降低30%；加入推而非抓等辅助技能可引入新行为模式，且未损害基线表现。

Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives. We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models. RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary

sections.text:
What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives.

We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models.

RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models, so that the policy learns to see what it needs for navigation.

In the same space it dreams what it wants: before every action a latent chain-of-thought predicts the representation of the scene a moment ahead. The dream is trained end-to-end with the policy as a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), with a next-representation prediction loss and a regularizer on its targets.

RepresentNav sets a new state of the art on VLNVerse, VLN-CE R2R, EVT-Bench, and two point-goal benchmarks, and its gains carry over to a physical robot amid clutter and moving people.

On VLNVerse fine-grained, RepresentNav achieves 83.80% success, outperforming the previous state of the art by 20.05 percentage points, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% with a single camera (+10.1).

With the same encoders, the self-constructed space clearly outperforms concatenating their outputs and learns to weight their layers unevenly, and a dream in it cuts collisions by a quarter.

A single dreamed latent decodes into the depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy of the scene a moment ahead, more accurately than pretrained encoders applied to the real future frame, although occupancy is never supervised, and the rollout tracks the robot's own motion over the next second: the dream emerges as a compact latent world model.

summary.en: The paper presents RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model that constructs a representation space from features across multiple vision foundation models. Its policy predicts a near-future scene representation before each action, trained jointly with the policy. The authors report state-of-the-art results on several navigation benchmarks and gains on a physical robot among clutter and moving people. They also report fewer collisions and that a dreamed latent can decode future depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy, although occupancy is not directly supervised.
summary.zh: 本文提出导航基础模型 RepresentNav，通过策略自身目标从多个视觉基础模型的不同深度特征构建表征空间，并在其中预测短时未来场景表征，以辅助动作决策。作者报告，该方法在多项导航基准上达到新的最佳结果，且收益延伸至有杂物和行人的实体机器人。文中还称，预测表征可减少碰撞，并能解码出未来场景的深度、语义和三维占用信息；占用信息未接受直接监督。

items.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space

sections.text:
Achieving effective locomotion on diverse terrestrial substrates can require subtle changes of limb kinematics. Biologically inspired legged robots (physical models of organisms) have shown impressive mobility on hard ground but suffer performance loss on unconsolidated granular materials like sand.

Because comprehensive limb-ground interaction models are lacking, optimal gaits on complex yielding terrain have been determined empirically.

To develop predictive models for legged devices and to provide hypotheses for biological locomotors, we systematically study the performance of SandBot, a small legged robot, on granular media as a function of gait parameters. High performance occurs only in a small region of parameter space.

A previously introduced kinematic model of the robot combined with a new anisotropic granular penetration force law predicts the speed. Performance on granular media is maximized when gait parameters minimize body acceleration and limb interference, and utilize solidification features of granular media.

summary.en: This study examines how gait parameters affect the speed of SandBot, a small legged robot, on granular media. The authors report that high performance occurs only within a small region of parameter space. They combine a previously introduced kinematic model with a new anisotropic granular penetration force law to predict speed. Their results indicate that performance is maximized when gait parameters reduce body acceleration and limb interference while taking advantage of granular solidification. The paper notes that optimal gaits on complex yielding terrain have generally been found empirically.
summary.zh: 本文通过系统改变 SandBot 小型足式机器人的步态参数，研究其在松散颗粒介质上的运动表现。作者指出，高性能只出现在较小的参数区域。研究将机器人运动学模型与新的各向异性颗粒穿透力定律结合，用于预测速度。实验表现表明，当步态参数能够减少机体加速度和肢体干扰，并利用颗粒介质的固化特性时，机器人在颗粒地面上的速度最高；文中也指出，复杂可变形地形的最优步态通常依赖经验确定。

items.title: The effect of limb kinematics on the speed of a legged robot on granular media

We introduce RynnUnify, a 16B unified embodied model that combines strong embodied understanding with long-horizon visual planning through interleaved video--language reasoning.

With capabilities spanning spatial reasoning, physical prediction, and grounding, RynnUnify connects an understanding of the physical world with visual anticipation of how it evolves across successive subtasks.

Building on these capabilities, we further develop an agentic extension through reinforcement learning to selectively use video predictions for reasoning about unobserved states and interaction outcomes. We also develop a world-action extension of the full RynnUnify model, translating its understanding and prediction capabilities into robot control.

To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Rynn-VP and Rynn-GEU for long-horizon visual planning and anticipatory reasoning. Experiments show that RynnUnify achieves the highest average embodied understanding score among the evaluated unified multimodal models and improves the Rynn-VP overall score by 9.75 points over Cosmos 3 Nano.

Its agentic extension improves the Rynn-GEU average by 6.0 points over direct reasoning, while the world-action extension achieves 51.5\% success on 20 selected composite RoboCasa365 tasks and 46.7\% average success across three real-robot tasks.

Together, these results establish RynnUnify as a shared foundation for embodied understanding, visual planning, and robot control, taking a step toward a unified embodied brain.

items.title: RynnUnify: Towards Unified Embodied Brain

sections.text:
Learned humanoid controllers are usually trained in one simulator and then checked in a second one before they go near hardware. We ask what that check says about command delay.

We train motion-tracking policies for a 24-joint humanoid on five motions taken from monocular video and test them in an independent CPU MuJoCo harness, which we first verify against the training model. Every policy completes its motion in at least 26 of 30 episodes under the training randomization.

With 40 ms of constant command delay, however, survival drops to 15% on average (0% - 45%), and the delay margin is only 20 - 30 ms. Randomizing the delay during training (0 - 50 ms) lifts survival at 40 ms to 95% on average (75% - 100%) and moves the margin to 50 - 70 ms.

A control arm trained for the same number of extra iterations without delay does not improve, so the gain comes from the randomization itself. This holds for all five motions with three training seeds each, and a policy trained in PhysX behaves the same way.

The price is slightly looser tracking (0.02 - 0.06 rad on four motions) and, for the most dynamic motion, less robustness to other perturbations. We also show that the first sim-to-sim gap we saw came from the harness, a missing floor and a wrong timestep, and not from the physics engines.

The 0 - 20 ms delay ranges common in locomotion training lie inside the margin an unrandomized tracker already has. The benefit comes from randomizing beyond it, so the range should be set from the robot's measured latency, and delay margin belongs next to other sim-to-sim metrics.

sections.text:
Model-predictive control with Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) provides a strong zero-shot goal-reaching planner, but it is only effective over short planning horizons. Hierarchical extensions attempt to bridge this gap by learning a macro planner to predict intermediate latent sub-goals to guide the micro planner.

In this work, we demonstrate that unconstrained latent sub-goal prediction is fundamentally flawed. A rigorous evaluation reveals that leading hierarchical macro planners routinely emit physically unrealisable sub-goals.

To resolve this, we introduce Metro-WM, a hierarchical framework that issues sub-goals by retrieving genuine states from prior experience rather than generating ungrounded latent vectors.

Specifically, Metro-WM constructs a graph whose vertices are observed frames from offline expert demonstrations or random-action trajectories, allowing frames from different episodes to be connected and stitched into routes to the goal.

Planning over the full graph also makes the system highly robust to execution errors: if the micro planner drifts off course, Metro-WM instantly finds a new optimal path from the current state.

Our experiments show that Metro-WM achieves superior long-horizon success rates of up to 37.33 percentage points over the strongest hierarchical baseline on the same world model while being up to 10.9 times faster, requiring both 13-56 times less offline compute and fewer tuned hyperparameters.

Additional analysis reveals that Metro-WM frequently finds shorter paths than the offline demonstrations, outperforms an oracle relying on the query's own demonstration on most benchmarks, and maintains robust performance under extremely sparse dataset conditions.

items.title: Metro-WM: Long-Horizon Latent Planning with Realisable Sub-Goals

Retargeting human motion to humanoids requires preserving motion semantics while accounting for the robot's physical constraints. Kinematic pipelines prescribe a robot trajectory through geometric matching, without establishing whether it can be executed under the robot's dynamics.

Prior physics-supervised neural methods train bidirectional full-sequence models on physics-refined kinematic trajectories, remaining tied to prescribed kinematic solutions and requiring noncausal context. We propose SMR, a streaming neural motion retargeter learned from semantic-conditioned physics experts.

We convert human motion into robot-aware task-space targets for body landmark positions, orientations, and velocities. Physics experts track these targets directly in simulation under contact, dynamics, and actuator constraints.

We train a single strictly causal Transformer on their executed state trajectories that complete the motion and pass semantic and physical validity checks. At each incoming frame, the student uses only current and past human observations to generate a robot motion reference for a downstream whole-body controller.

Experiments demonstrate that semantic-conditioned physics experts generate motion with higher semantic fidelity and physical validity than direct optimization-based retargeting, while the resulting streaming retargeter achieves improved closed-loop performance over kinematic and physics-refined baselines under a common whole-body controller.

items.title: SMR: Learning streaming motion retargeting for humanoids from human semantic

sections.text:
As humanoid robots move from research laboratories toward deployment in human-centered environments such as homes, hospitals, and warehouses, safe operation around nearby people and objects becomes a fundamental requirement.

Safety filters have emerged as a promising technique to address this challenge by providing mathematical guarantees that generated control actions do not result in collisions. This paper shows that these guarantees hold only when the safety parameters are configured correctly.

However, correct parameter configurations are task- and environment-specific, and no general method exists to determine them across diverse deployments. As a result, safety filters shipped with humanoid robots can fail after deployment in specific scenarios.

We show that attackers can exploit these failures through only normal user interactions without any additional privileges or capabilities. To demonstrate this risk, we present goal insertion attacks and develop SIREN, an automated tool that identifies vulnerable inserting goals for a given task and environment.

Experimental results show that SIREN identifies attacks in all vulnerable scenarios in the SPARK dataset. Compared with a baseline approach, SIREN discovers three times as many attacks. We also show that SIREN is able to generate attacks against a real humanoid and cause it to collide while executing tasks.

These results demonstrate that current safety filters introduce exploitable vulnerabilities that can cause safety violations, which reveals that existing safety mechanisms can themselves become a source of safety risk for humanoid robots.

items.title: Not an Accident: Exploiting Safety Filter Inadequacy in Humanoid Robots

Robot foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, motivating low-cost offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality.

We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion?

To test this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion.

We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs).

Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs).With $S^2$, we extend PRH to robotics and make sensorimotor alignment measurable, offering a low-cost, representation-level view of robot foundation models that closed-loop success rates alone cannot reveal.

items.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success

A coarse stage assigns visual-semantic scores to candidate headings on a 0-10 scale; a fine stage measures symbolic compatibility between observed objects, room context, and the goal prior. Steering robot foundation models (RFMs) toward new task variants or user-preferred behaviors remains challenging, often requiring additional robot demonstrations, task-specific fine-tuning, or long-context conditioning. We present WAM-TTT, a test-time training framework for steering world action models from raw human videos.

Rather than treating human videos as trajectories to imitate, WAM-TTT absorbs them into a lightweight adaptive memory inside a frozen WAM through self-supervised video prediction.

To make this memory useful for control, we introduce a meta-training stage that aligns human demonstrations with robot behaviors using paired human-robot data and a key--value memory reconstruction objective. At test time, only unlabeled human videos are required to adapt the memory, while the pretrained WAM remains frozen.

This enables efficient and reusable steering without robot actions, human-side annotations, or task-specific fine-tuning, while preserving the generalization ability of the foundation model.

Extensive experiments show that WAM-TTT consistently outperforms in-context human-video conditioning baselines across diverse manipulation tasks and generalization settings.

items.title: WAM-TTT: Steering World-Action Models by Watching Human Play at Test Time

sections.text:
Deep Reinforcement Learning policies can produce nonsmooth action oscillations that hinder deployment on physical robots. Existing architectural and penalty-based approaches seek spatial smoothness by directly reducing sensitivity to changes in state inputs, but their broad constraints can degrade task performance as stronger smoothing is pursued.

Temporal regularization instead constrains action differences along observed transitions, but has been considered unable to provide the spatial smoothness needed under observation noise.

We revisit this assumption by proving that the temporal penalty bounds the expected action differences between current states sharing a next state, revealing a spatial effect that empirically extends to spatial smoothness.

Building on this finding, we propose Conditioning for Action using only Temporal Smoothness (CATS), which combines a temporal penalty with linear ramp-up. We highlight temporal regularization's ability to provide spatial smoothness while better preserving task performance than explicit spatial regularization.

Through linear ramp-up, CATS allows the policy to learn rewarding behavior before progressively smoothing its actions, improving return preservation and both temporal and spatial smoothness.

Experiments in both simulation and the real world show that CATS substantially reduces action oscillation without degrading task performance, with little computational overhead.

items.title: Revisiting Temporal Regularization for Smooth Control in Deep Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Unrecognized anomalies in critical infrastructure can rapidly cascade into catastrophic physical or operational failures. Current anomaly detection approaches often rely on direct access to the monitored system by utilizing onboard sensors, such as motor encoders, to detect anomalous states.

However, legacy hardware often lacks these sensors, or strict security protocols may prohibit access altogether. We therefore present AWARE, a world model framework that is capable of anomaly detection using only external camera monitoring via system dynamics estimation and state prediction.

Evaluated across 240 real-world robotic crane trajectories, including payload collisions and motor degradations, AWARE demonstrates a 26% improvement in anomaly classification over our strongest baseline under noisy, camera-only state estimation.

Furthermore, the inferred dynamics parameter can be decoded to identify the source of faults, localizing the degrading motor with 88% accuracy.

items.title: Adaptive World-Models for Anomaly Recognition (AWARE): A Framework for Robot Dynamics Prediction and Introspection

Embodied AI and robotic systems increasingly depend on scalable, diverse, and physically grounded 3D content for simulation-based training and real-world deployment.

While 3D generative modeling has advanced rapidly, embodied applications impose requirements far beyond visual realism: generated objects must carry kinematic structure and material properties, scenes must support interaction and task execution, and the resulting content must bridge the gap between simulation and reality.

This survey reviews 3D generation for embodied AI and organizes the literature around three roles that 3D generation plays in embodied systems.

In Data Generator, 3D generation produces simulation-ready objects and assets, including articulated, physically grounded, and deformable content for downstream interaction; in Simulation Environments, it constructs interactive and task-oriented worlds, spanning structure-aware, controllable, and agentic scene generation; and in Sim2Real Bridge, it supports digital twin reconstruction, data augmentation, and synthetic demonstrations for downstream robot learning and real-world transfer.

We also show that the field is shifting from visual realism toward interaction readiness, and we identify the main bottlenecks, including limited physical annotations, the gap between geometric quality and physical validity, fragmented evaluation, and the persistent sim-to-real divide, that must be addressed for 3D generation to become a dependable foundation for embodied intelligence.

Our project page is at https://3dgen4robot.github.io.

items.title: 3D Generation for Embodied AI and Robotic Simulation: A Survey

Data-driven robots must learn to avoid collisions with as few demonstrations as possible to avoid collecting large datasets of destructive collision examples.

We explore whole-body proximity sensors as inductive biases for learning reflexive collision-dodging behavior and find that lossy sensors with low resolution were stronger biases than high-resolution coverage. We also found that, perhaps unintuitively, anticipating when and where contact happens on the body of a robot reduced its learning sample efficiency.

We investigated eight candidate representations in a reinforcement learning environment, which included latent compression, future contact anticipation, lossy corruption, and privileged state estimation.

The candidate representations were tested by training over 200 humanoid robots to play a simplified version of dodgeball end-to-end under an intentionally constrained sample and compute budget.

Real-world reinforcement learning has enabled contact-rich manipulation tasks to be trained directly on physical robots, but unsafe interactions during online learning remain a key barrier to practical deployment.

We propose Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning (SEVI), a framework for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world policy learning. SEVI introduces an Evidential Safety Critic that estimates both future constraint-violation risk and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass.

During online learning, SEVI evaluates each task-policy action before execution; if the action is predicted to be unsafe or the prediction is insufficiently supported by evidence, SEVI overrides it with an offline-trained recovery policy that guides the robot toward a lower-risk region.

We evaluate SEVI on two simulated manipulation tasks and a real-world USB insertion task under in-distribution and distribution-shifted conditions. Across task-learning and safety-critic baselines, SEVI achieves the strongest trajectory-level safety prediction, the highest final task success, and the lowest unsafe-event counts.

SEVI also reduces unsafe events by 13.4 to 57.1 percent relative to recovery-based safe RL while preserving low-latency execution-time filtering. The project page is available at: https://sevi-safe.github.io/

items.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists.

We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP.

Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.

items.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point

sections.text:
In medical robotics, data-driven soft-tissue shape control requires deforming tissue toward desired morphologies through sequential physical interactions.

This challenge is particularly important in microscale manipulation, where localized deformation is difficult to observe, represent, and control, while physics-based models can be computationally expensive and difficult to adapt to realistic environments.

Optical coherence tomography (OCT) provides high-resolution volumetric perception of tissue deformation, but target-conditioned control requires effective representations of both observed and desired tissue states.

In this work, we introduce an OCT-guided data-driven framework for tissue shape control, learned from user-guided demonstrations and executed with closed-loop OCT feedback.

We study full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud representations, with or without residual conditioning, using deterministic (Explicit) and generative diffusion (Diffusion) policies.

Across 12 configurations and 576 phantom rollouts on 3-DoF depth and 6-DoF directional tasks, OCT-derived 3D representations support both Explicit and Diffusion policies, with performance depending on representation and residual conditioning.

Residual conditioning reduces directional Shape RMSE from 0.748 to 0.555 mm for full-volume Diffusion, while voxelized point-cloud Explicit with residuals achieves 0.534 mm for depth and 0.443 mm for directional control, with comparable accuracy at intermediate unseen targets and consistent performance across deployments.

We further evaluate the framework in 60 ex vivo porcine rollouts, extending to biological tissue with final geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. These results establish volumetric OCT as current and goal representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control across deterministic and generative action models.

items.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control

Segmenting robot demonstration data into disjoint temporal and semantic subsegments is valuable for learning, cleaning, retrieval, and analysis. Segmentation is often performed manually in a tedious and error prone process.

Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have the potential for automating this process, but directly ingesting raw multi camera video streams into MLLMs can be costly and can quickly exhaust context windows. In this paper, we introduce KiRoSe (Kinematics for Robot Segmentation), a novel framework that focuses on the companion stream of robot kinematic data.

Inspired by the principle of classical entropy coding, such as Huffman coding, where frequently occurring symbols are represented more compactly, we propose Sparse Motion Tokens (SMTs), a discrete kinematic vocabulary designed to compactly represent recurring, temporally localized motion patterns, which we refer to as kinematic events.

SMTs are learned by encoding kinematic trajectories with temporal segment supervision and quantizing the resulting features. We use increasingly available robot demonstration subtask annotations to supervise an open language model to interpret the resulting token sequences.

Evaluation against human labeled segmentation shows that KiRoSe can substantially outperform baseline segmentation methods in F1 quality and transfers zero shot to unseen robot embodiments and egocentric human motion, while preserving the language models open vocabulary knowledge.

Beyond segmentation, KiRoSe tracks task progress on an unseen robot and detects when an action is being reversed.(website: https://berkeleyautomation.github.io/kirose/)

items.title: KiRoSe: Using Kinematic Data for Efficient Segmentation of Robot Demonstrations

Ultrasound imaging is highly operator-dependent, motivating robotic systems that reproduce expert scanning skills consistently. These skills involve coordinated interpretation of anatomical landmarks, ultrasound images, and probe-tissue interactions that are difficult to encode in hand-designed control strategies.

Imitation learning offers an alternative, but its observation and action representations should reflect the anatomically structured nature of scanning. We propose an anatomy-anchored imitation-learning framework that combines anatomy-guided probe placement with learned ultrasound navigation.

The placement module identifies a task-specific anatomical starting point from external visual observations and establishes the initial probe pose as the reference frame for scanning.

A flow-based policy then generates scanning motions from anchor-relative probe poses, ultrasound images, probe-mounted camera views, and contact forces, while a termination head predicts task completion. This avoids continuous reliance on third-person vision and reduces dependence on the robot-patient configuration.

A handheld acquisition platform enables multimodal demonstrations to be collected during natural freehand scanning without a robot. On 16 unseen participants, task success reaches 96%, 94%, 88%, and 94% for kidney, gallbladder, and liver standard-plane acquisition and radial artery sweeping, respectively.

Compared with a fine-tuned pi_0 model, success on the abdominal tasks improves by 10-42 percentage points, with lower time-to-target, peak contact force, and trajectory jerk. Ablations support the complementary roles of anatomical anchoring, egocentric vision, and force feedback.

End-to-end trials with automatic placement achieve 90-100% success, and the policies transfer without retraining to a second robot with 83-100% success.

items.title: From Freehand Demonstrations to Autonomous Robotic Ultrasound: An Anatomy-Anchored Learning Framework

Although the advancement of vision-language models (VLMs) has endowed robots with enhanced environmental understanding and task reasoning, a comprehensive evaluation methodology is important to advance the integration of VLMs in robotic navigation and manipulation.

However, current benchmarks lack a comprehensive method to evaluate diverse robotic tasks, and evaluation metrics remain relatively constrained, making it difficult to assess the embodied capabilities of VLMs in a thorough and fine-grained manner.

To address this issue, we propose RMMBench, an evaluation benchmark that requires robots to understand language instructions and perform long-horizon tasks in continuous spaces.

RMMBench seamlessly integrates high- and low-level embodied tasks into a unified framework, constructing a "navigation-manipulation" task suite comprising 70 canonical task scenarios that range from localized manipulation to long-horizon composite navigation.

The results reveal that leading VLMs still face major challenges in spatial localization when performing mobile manipulation tasks, and also highlight the necessity of enhancing the spatial perception capability of robots during long-horizon interactions. RMMBench can be accessed at https://mxxq-stack.github.io/rmmbench-project/

items.title: RMMBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Robotic Mobile Manipulation

Robot-assisted dressing is particularly challenging due to narrow openings and articulated body parts. Even small errors in the relative pose between the body part and garment opening can cause snagging, missed insertion, or incomplete dressing.

To address these challenges, we formulate dressing as a geometry-aware insertion problem that represents task-relevant spatial relationships between the body part and object opening, rather than relying on the full deformable-object state.

Based on this formulation, we propose a Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework combining a staged curriculum, which progressively guides the policy from coarse alignment to insertion and final placement, with a finger-wise insertion soft gate that provides continuous feedback on individual finger insertion progress and helps suppress premature insertion.

We evaluate the framework on rigid and deformable bracelet dressing tasks through component ablations, systematic variations in the initial hand pose, and closed-loop execution of the learned policies on a real robotic system. On the post-training deformable evaluation, the full method reaches 84.7 +- 1.2% success.

The insertion gate accounts for the largest gain, and adding the curriculum on top of that gate reaches the top score. On a mannequin hand the same full policy succeeds on 15/20 real-robot trials.

Generating physically stable 3D structures from visual specifications requires resolving geometric ambiguity while accounting for physical interactions among objects. We present StackGen3D, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. Our approach consists of two stages.

First, we develop a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures.

Second, we train a conditional flow-matching model on this dataset to capture the multimodal distribution of block configurations consistent with the target silhouettes. At inference time, lightweight geometric selection and refinement reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation.

Preliminary experiments show that the PI-GNN generalizes from simple stacks to complex structures substantially better than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron. For structure generation, Best-of-10 selection improves physical stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while achieving a silhouette IoU of 0.970.

These results highlight the potential of combining relational physical reasoning, scalable data curation, and conditional generative modeling for creative 3D assembly. Project website: [https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/](https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/)

items.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes

To evaluate the frontier, we must measure models not by what they say, but by what they can engineer and build in grounded physical environments. We introduce ArtifactArena, an open-ended platform where models face a physically grounded hardware-software co-design challenge: engineering fully functional robots to compete in a simulated arena.

We evaluate a frontier model's zero-shot, verifier guided refinement, and open-ended physical design capabilities through three harnesses that refine their bot artifacts based on text descriptions, physics simulator feedback, and gameplay data.

We benchmark these capabilities with an Elo ranking of frontier models derived from head-to-head tournaments between their artifacts.

By releasing this framework and tournament infrastructure for ongoing community submissions, we establish a living, non-saturating testbed to continuously measure the expanding limits of open-ended intelligence in the physical world. Please visit https://artifactarena.ai for more information.

items.title: ArtifactArena: Evaluating Models by What They Build in the Physical World
